title: Integrated Bibliometric and Computational Analysis of Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Finance
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into financial services presents a transformative opportunity to advance sustainability goals, yet a systematic understanding of its current state and impact is essential. This review aims to synthesize existing literature on AI applications within the financial sector, emphasizing their role in promoting sustainability and environmental, social, and governance principles. The study screened 3507 articles published in ABS‐ranked journals between 2020 and 2025 on AI and sustainability, narrowing the sample to a core corpus of 181 articles for mixed‐method analysis combining bibliometric techniques with Python‐based data analytics. Synthesized findings reveal significant research prevalence across AI sub‐domains such as machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing within sustainable finance contexts. Although literature supports the potential of AI to act both as an enabler of financial inclusion and as a tool for environmental impact assessment, variations in study contexts suggest a need for further standardized research to fully quantify its long‐term efficacy.

title: The impact of real-digital integration on green economic efficiency in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
summary: Abstract The integration of the real economy and the digital economy is a crucial driver for regional high-quality development and green transformation. Using panel data from 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YEB) during 2006–2022, this study employs the patent co-classification method and super-efficiency SBM model to measure real-digital integration (RD) and green economic efficiency (GEE), empirically examining their relationship. The results show that: (1) RD levels across cities show an upward trend but with widening regional disparities exhibiting a Matthew Effect; GEE follows a spatial pattern of upstream > downstream > midstream. (2) RD is significantly associated with higher GEE. (3) This association operates through three channels: green finance development, green innovation capacity, and artificial intelligence applications. (4) The relationship is stronger in upstream and downstream cities, non-resource-based cities, post-2015, and service-oriented cities. These findings offer policy references for governments, enterprises, and financial institutions to advance green transformation through RD.

title: Powering the green transition with FinTech and AI from a green finance perspective
summary: Research at the intersection of green finance, FinTech, and artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly, yet its conceptual structure and transmission mechanisms remain fragmented. This study combines a systematic review and bibliometric mapping of 139 Scopus-indexed journal articles published between 2020 and 2025 whose titles explicitly connect green finance with FinTech and/or artificial intelligence. The TITLE-based search captures the explicit-title core of this literature and does not provide exhaustive coverage of adjacent research. Bibliometric analyses, including performance analysis, keyword co-occurrence, country co-authorship, and co-citation mapping, are integrated with a four-channel framework: information & transparency, risk assessment & pricing, financial inclusiont & access, and RegTech & infrastructure. The findings reveal rapid growth after 2023 and strong geographic concentration in China. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies four thematic communities: digital infrastructures, the sustainability–FinTech nexus, carbon markets and financial connectedness, and China-focused policy transition. The synthesis identifies risk assessment & pricing as the most empirically developed channel. Information & transparency are prominent but less consistently validated, while direct evidence on RegTech outcomes and micro-level access to green finance remains limited. These imbalances are interpreted in relation to data availability, measurement tractability, and institutional context. The review links bibliometric structures to proposed transmission mechanisms and develops a research agenda centered on causal identification, measurement consistency, and cross-institutional validation.

title: Edukasi Transformasi Digital UMKM dalam Penggunaan OCTO Merchant untuk Pemberdayaan Ekonomi Lokal
summary: Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) play an important role in the economy, but there are still many MSMEs that do not understand the use of technology. In the era of digitalization, digital transformation is necessary to empower the local economy, one of which is the use of the OCTO Merchant application. OCTO Merchant is designed to facilitate non-cash transactions, increase business administration efficiency, and provide real-time access to financial reports. The research was conducted using a qualitative descriptive method with a literature study approach and participatory observation in digital education seminars. The research results show that the use of digital technology such as OCTO Merchant can help MSMEs overcome operational limitations, increase transaction security, and support competitiveness in the digital economy era. However, obstacles such as low technological literacy, traditional habits, and limited resources are challenges in the process of adopting this technology. It is hoped that ongoing socialization and education will be able to encourage MSME players to be better prepared to face digital transformation and contribute to local and national economic growth.

title: How Does Computing Infrastructure Improve Corporate ESG Performance? Evidence from Chinese Manufacturing Firms
summary: Computing infrastructure has become a critical underlying resource for the digital development and sustainable transformation of manufacturing firms. Using panel data from Chinese listed manufacturing firms from 2011 to 2024, this study employs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the impact of computing infrastructure development on corporate ESG performance. The results show that computing infrastructure development significantly improves firms’ ESG performance, and this finding remains robust across a series of robustness checks. Further analysis indicates that this effect operates primarily through reducing internal transaction costs, optimizing human capital structure, and promoting digital transformation, while being strengthened by managerial capabilities and the level of regional green finance development. This study extends research on computing infrastructure and corporate ESG from the perspective of underlying digital infrastructure, providing empirical evidence on how digital resources contribute to corporate sustainability and offering implications for optimizing computing infrastructure deployment.

title: Caught in ESG trap? Evidence from earnings pressure by examining CEO overconfidence and pay slice
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how firms balance long-term environmental, social and corporate governance (ESG) commitments with more tactical ESG actions aimed at managing capital-market expectations, particularly through dialogues with securities analysts. Drawing on a managerial-cognitive perspective, it investigates how CEO overconfidence and CEO pay slice shape ESG decisions under varying levels of earnings pressure. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel of 14,697 firm-year observations from S&P 1500 firms over 2003–2024, the study estimates OLS regressions of tactical ESG investing on earnings pressure and its interactions with CEO overconfidence and pay slice, and applies time-series clustering to firms’ ESG score trajectories to identify distinct behavioral patterns and industry-driven groupings. Findings The analysis finds that overconfident CEOs are more likely to pursue long-term ESG strategies and resist short-term tactical ESG responses under earnings pressure. In contrast, a high CEO pay slice is associated with increased tactical ESG engagement to meet analyst expectations. Time series clustering reveals industry-driven ESG behavior patterns, reinforcing the need to align governance mechanisms with executive traits and contextual factors in ESG strategy formulation. Practical implications Sustainable development cannot be advanced merely by increasing the visibility or quantity of ESG activity; governance systems must protect the time horizon, substance and accountability of sustainability commitments. Boards and sustainability committees, compensation committees, investors and regulators should therefore reward durable, outcome-oriented ESG implementation over easily adjustable actions that mainly relieve short-term market pressure. Social implications By distinguishing tactical from strategic ESG engagement, the study shows how short-term capital-market pressure may weaken the durability and substance of the corporate sustainability commitments − the sustained investments in capabilities, stakeholder relationships and environmental and social practices − on which social resilience, environmental protection and accountable governance ultimately depend. Originality/value This study reconceptualizes CEO overconfidence as a context-dependent moderator of ESG responses to earnings pressure rather than a simple driver of ESG scores, identifies CEO pay slice as a temporal incentive mechanism and introduces shape-based time-series clustering to uncover the structure of ESG evolution for sustainable development.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reducing Agency Costs and Improving Corporate Governance Efficiency: An Analytical Study
summary: This study aimed to analyze the role of artificial intelligence in reducing agency costs and improving the efficiency of institutional control, considering the rapid developments in the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies in auditing, control management risk, and corporate governance. The study addressed a research problem arising from the limited theoretical foundation and the scarcity of Arabic literature and research examining the relationship between artificial intelligence applications and agency costs, particularly their three dimensions: monitoring costs, bonding costs, and residual loss. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach and an inductive analytical approach by reviewing and analyzing relevant literature, previous studies, and specialized reports published during the period 2020–2026. The study concluded that artificial intelligence could contribute to the reducing of agency costs by enhancing continuous monitoring, improving the quality and timeliness of information, reducing information asymmetry, supporting decision-making, and enabling the early detection of errors, fraud, and managerial deviations. The findings also indicated that artificial intelligence applications in auditing, control, and risk management facilitate a shift from ex post control to proactive and intelligent control, thereby enhancing institutional control efficiency, supporting risk prediction, activating early-warning systems, and promoting more efficient use of resources. Furthermore, artificial intelligence can strengthen governance, accountability, and compliance and contribute to limiting managerial opportunism. However, its use also creates new challenges related to data protection, algorithmic bias, transparency, legal responsibility, and overreliance on intelligent systems. The study concluded that realizing the full benefits of artificial intelligence requires an integrated digital governance framework that balances automation with human oversight and ensures transparency, accountability, and data protection.

title: BETWEEN READINESS AND RISK: DESIGNING DECISION-MAKING MODELS FOR ADVANCED COMPANIES IN A DYNAMIC DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: Our study examines institutional innovation management systems in the context of global digital transformation. The primary objective was to establish theoretical and methodological foundations and to offer practical recommendations for enhancing innovation management mechanisms—an endeavor that requires integrating digital resources with risk management. The study yielded several key findings: first, the development of assessment frameworks to gauge institutional readiness for digital transformation using DP and DM indicators; second, the adoption of process transformation models, specifically the Osterwalder model; third, the application of methodological approaches to identify project threats and opportunities; and fourth, the implementation of specific systems or mechanisms for risk management. This study was conducted at leading institutions in the North Caucasus region.

title: Patient Capital and Corporate Green Technological Innovation: The Roles of Capital Sources and Corporate Governance
summary: Green technological innovation requires capital that can tolerate delayed returns and long development cycles, yet the sustainability implications of capital horizon remain underexplored. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2008 to 2024, this study examines the association between patient capital and corporate green technological innovation. Patient capital is operationalized as a multidimensional composite of ownership-based and financing-based dimensions. Firm and year fixed-effects estimates show a positive association between patient capital and green technological innovation. Source decomposition indicates that the financing-based component is positive and statistically significant, whereas the ownership-based component is positive but statistically insignificant; a formal test shows that the financing-based coefficient is significantly larger. Corporate governance strengthens the association. Distributional tests indicate some upper-tail heterogeneity but do not support a uniformly increasing association across quantiles. Threshold analysis suggests that the positive association becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero at high levels of patient capital. These findings highlight the importance of aligning capital horizon, financing structure, and governance with the long-cycle requirements of corporate low-carbon innovation.

title: The Importance of Supply Chain Strategy in Logistics Service Delivery: An Exploratory Study from the Libyan Perspective
summary: This study examines how supply chain management can enhance logistics service delivery in Libya. Drawing on recent literature and comparative evidence from the MENA region and Africa, it explores how supply chain strategies influence logistics performance in developing countries facing infrastructure, regulatory, and operational challenges. A qualitative approach is adopted, synthesizing academic studies, case examples, and regional analyses to demonstrate how supply chains can improve logistics services. The results show that Libya faces significant infrastructure deficiencies, fragmented regulatory frameworks, and conflict-related disruptions, which hinder effective strategic integration. However, adopting supply chain management practices, effective leadership, and partnerships can help develop competitive advantages. The study identifies significant gaps in logistics infrastructure, especially in ports and supply chain systems, while noting Libya’s strategically important geographic location. Recommendations focus on strengthening institutions, investing in digital technology, developing a skilled workforce, and improving regulatory and policy frameworks to enhance supply chain resilience and effectiveness. This research contributes to the limited work on supply chain management in conflict-affected developing countries. It provides practical insights for policymakers, logistics experts, and international partners working in Libya and similar contexts.

title: Declaratory commitments and practical gaps: understanding equal treatment in Estonian corporate social responsible practice
summary: Abstract Estonian companies increasingly recognise the importance of corporate social responsibility (CSR), yet their understanding of its substantive link to equal treatment remains limited. Although employers often include equality principles in internal policies, such commitments are largely declaratory and reflect a narrow understanding of equal treatment, often reducing it to the gender pay gap. This article examines the intersection between CSR and equal treatment within international, EU, and Estonian regulatory frameworks. Modern sustainability standards, including in the European area the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive 1 and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive 2 , have transformed CSR from voluntary practice into a framework of binding obligations, positioning equal treatment as a core component of ethical governance, legal compliance, and long-term competitiveness. However, the multiplicity of regulatory requirements complicates implementation and creates interpretative challenges for employers. Using a doctrinal methodology, the study maps global and domestic legal norms to clarify the legal foundations of employer social responsibility and the role of equal treatment within it. The analysis reveals significant gaps: Estonia lacks empirical data on how companies implement equality-related CSR standards in practice, while employers’ conceptual understanding of those standards remains limited. The paper concludes that effective implementation requires clearer doctrinal guidance, stronger institutional support, and more proactive corporate engagement. It calls for future empirical research to assess Estonian companies’ knowledge, organisational practices, and capacity to integrate equal treatment into everyday corporate governance.

title: Sustainable Mining Practices for Environmental Protection and Public Health: An Empirical Study
summary: Research Background: Mining is fundamental to economic development because it supplies minerals and raw materials required for infrastructure, manufacturing, energy production, transportation, construction, and emerging technologies. However, conventional mining practices are frequently associated with land degradation, deforestation, biodiversity loss, soil erosion, excessive water consumption, contamination of surface and groundwater, dust generation, greenhouse-gas emissions, and large volumes of mine waste. These environmental pressures may also create significant public-health concerns for mine workers and surrounding communities through exposure to particulate matter, heavy metals, contaminated water, noise, and occupational hazards. Sustainable mining therefore requires an integrated approach that balances mineral production and economic benefits with environmental protection, resource efficiency, worker safety, community health, and social responsibility. Research Problem / Research Gap: Although mining companies increasingly adopt environmental management systems, cleaner technologies, waste-management strategies, mine rehabilitation, renewable energy, and corporate social responsibility programmes, considerable variation remains in their implementation and effectiveness. Existing studies often examine environmental pollution, occupational health, mining technology, or community impacts separately. Comparatively fewer empirical studies integrate sustainable mining practices, environmental protection, and public-health outcomes within a single analytical framework. Furthermore, evidence is required regarding which sustainable practices have the greatest potential to simultaneously reduce ecological damage and health risks. Research Objectives: The study aims to assess the contribution of sustainable mining practices to environmental protection and public health. Specifically, it seeks to examine the effects of pollution-control practices, sustainable water management, mine-waste management, cleaner and energy-efficient technologies, land rehabilitation, occupational health and safety practices, and community engagement on environmental and health outcomes. It also aims to identify implementation barriers and recommend strategies for strengthening sustainability within the mining sector. Methodology: The proposed study will adopt a quantitative, cross-sectional empirical research design, supported where appropriate by qualitative observations. Primary data may be collected from approximately 200 respondents, including mining employees, managers, environmental and safety personnel, healthcare/public-health professionals, and members of mining-affected communities. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale will measure major study constructs. Secondary information may be obtained from peer-reviewed literature, government reports, environmental assessments, and mining sustainability reports. Data analysis may include descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, correlation analysis, multiple regression, ANOVA, and, where appropriate, structural equation modelling (SEM). Expected Key Findings: The study is expected to demonstrate that effective pollution control, responsible water use, scientific mine-waste management, cleaner technology, land restoration, strong occupational safety systems, and community participation are positively associated with environmental protection and improved public-health outcomes. Strong environmental governance and regulatory compliance are also expected to enhance these relationships. Research Implications: The research may provide evidence for mining companies, policymakers, environmental regulators, public-health authorities, and local communities regarding the development of integrated mining sustainability strategies. It may support a transition from compliance-oriented environmental management toward preventive, technology-enabled, health-sensitive, and community-inclusive mining practices.

title: The Corporate Governance Implications of Presidentialism
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has pushed the United States into a new system of public governance, “Presidentialism,” which gives unprecedented economic regulatory power and enforcement power to the President. Compensation arrangements designed to align shareholder and managerial interests now give the President additional power to obtain corporate compliance with preferred policy positions because of the concentrated firm-specific pecuniary stakes of managers and directors. In the name of protecting the democracy against authoritarian over-reach, we need new corporate governance institutions that insulate decision-makers from this pecuniary pressure, here, a Public Integrity Committee at the board level, compensated without stock and protected through staggered terms. Similarly, the exposure of asset managers to pressure over their stewardship voting strategies call for divestment of voting authority to decentralized but autonomous voting offices. This preserves the efficiency of centralized fund administration and portfolio assembly and marketing while divesting the asset manager of voting authority that makes it a potential target of Presidentialist pressure.

title: Long‐Run Relationships Between Green Finance, Artificial Intelligence, Women in Management, and Carbon Emissions: Evidence From Japan
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between the production of scientific knowledge in the field of artificial intelligence, the issuance of green bonds, the presence of women in senior and middle management in Japan, and carbon emissions. The model includes economic growth and trade openness as key macroeconomic factors that may influence environmental performance. The empirical analysis employs a Fourier theory‐based approach that considers possible soft structural changes. The results indicate that scientific publications in the field of artificial intelligence, the issuance of green bonds, and the presence of female leadership may have a negative correlation with carbon emissions. Conversely, economic growth and trade openness appear to be positively associated with CO 2 emissions. These results suggest that technological know‐how, sustainable financing, and inclusive governance can be considered complementary mechanisms for environmental sustainability. From a policy perspective, these results highlight the importance of actually applying the scientific capabilities of artificial intelligence, strengthening the green bond market, and supporting the effective presence of women in decision‐making processes. By addressing these elements within a common empirical framework, this study contributes to a more comprehensive assessment of the relationships between SDGs 5, 7, 9, and 13.

title: Exploring sustainable finance and ESG integration in commercial bank
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how senior executives in Nepalese commercial banks conceptualize and implement sustainable finance, with a focus on integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative phenomenological approach was adopted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight purposively selected executives, and data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s seven-step thematic framework using axial coding. Findings The study reveals varied understandings of sustainable finance, ranging from corporate social responsibility initiatives to ESG risk integration. Leadership commitment and personal values drive progress, while regulatory uncertainty, limited ESG tools and profitability pressures hinder implementation. A fragmented approach emerges, reflecting the tension between short-term financial goals and long-term sustainability. Research limitations/implications The focus on commercial banks limits generalizability across other financial institutions, but the findings highlight important directions for future research on ESG integration in frontier markets. Practical implications The study provides actionable insights for banks to strengthen leadership engagement, build internal ESG capacity and design policies that integrate sustainability into financial decisions. Social implications By highlighting the role of banks in addressing climate change, governance challenges and community development, the research shows how sustainable finance can promote inclusive and responsible growth. Originality/value This study contributes originality by exploring sustainable finance through the leadership perspective in a frontier market context, offering novel insights into ESG integration in Nepalese commercial banking and advocating systemic reforms for sustainable banking practices.

title: Corporate Governance and Political Embeddedness: A Systematic Review of Royal Family Affiliation, Earnings Management, and Audit Quality
summary: This systematic literature review examines the growing significance of royal family affiliation in shaping earnings management (EM) within emerging markets, particularly in contexts characterized by concentrated ownership and strong political influence. The study aims to synthesize existing literature, identify dominant methodological trends, and highlight directions for future research. The review addresses three key questions: (1) How does royal family affiliation influence earnings management in politically connected environments? (2) What methodological approaches are commonly employed to examine this relationship? and (3) What underexplored areas remain in the literature regarding governance mechanisms and audit fees?. The review synthesizes 40 studies published between 2010 and 2025, sourced from major academic databases including Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using VOSviewer to identify thematic patterns and research trends. The findings indicate a predominance of quantitative research approaches, with limited use of qualitative and mixed-method designs. The review emphasizes the need for further investigation into the moderating role of audit fees as indicators of external monitoring and audit quality, and their influence on the governance role of royal family board members. Additionally, the study identifies underexplored determinants, including board experience, ownership structure, and regulatory frameworks, particularly within emerging markets. The review advocates for a multidimensional approach to understanding earnings management and calls for more comprehensive empirical testing of governance mechanisms in politically embedded corporate environments.

title: Shareholder connection network and corporate supply chain resilience: evidence from Chinese listed firms
summary: Purpose Supply chain resilience is crucial for firms navigating an increasingly volatile global environment, yet the factors that enhance it remain underexplored. Existing literature offers conflicting views on the role of shareholder connection networks, debating whether they foster governance synergy or promote competitive collusion. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share listed companies during the period 2012–2023, our study investigates the impact of the shareholder connection network as a circular-oriented relational intangible (circular intellectual capital) on supply chain resilience as a capability enabling circular transformation. Findings We find that such networks significantly enhance supply chain resilience. This positive effect operates through two primary channels: reducing operational risk and improving information disclosure quality relevant to inter-firm transparency, which in turn foster inter-firm trust and collaboration supporting regenerative, closed-loop supply chains. The impact is more pronounced among firms in growth or decline stages and in settings characterized by lower levels of marketization or less intense competition. Originality/value Our findings offer practical insights for managers to better understand the role of such networks in risk management and supply chain governance, aid firms in partner selection, and inform policymakers seeking to promote supply chain resilience and circular-oriented value creation through high-quality development.

title: Peran Literasi Keuangan Hijau Dalam Mendukung Implementasi Green Accounting Melalui Corporate Social Responsibility Pada Pelaku Umkm di Kabupaten Pekalongan
summary: Perkembangan Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) dalam klaster manufaktur batik Kabupaten Pekalongan berperan sebagai katalis vital bagi pertumbuhan ekonomi regional, namun sekaligus memicu degradasi lingkungan akibat pengolahan limbah pewarnaan yang tidak memadai. Literasi keuangan hijau yang kurang memadai di kalangan pengusaha UMKM diidentifikasi sebagai kendala utama yang menghambat penerapan akuntansi hijau sebagai kerangka akuntabilitas lingkungan. Studi ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi pengaruh literasi keuangan hijau terhadap implementasi akuntansi hijau, dengan menetapkan Tanggung Jawab Sosial Perusahaan (CSR) sebagai variabel mediasi di antara UMKM batik di Kabupaten Pekalongan. Desain korelasional kuantitatif digunakan dengan pendekatan berbasis survei pada 100 responden yang dipilih melalui purposive sampling. Data primer yang dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert lima poin diolah menggunakan Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) melalui SmartPLS 4.0. Temuan empiris mengkonfirmasi bahwa literasi keuangan hijau memberikan dampak positif dan signifikan secara statistik baik pada CSR (beta = 0,412; p < 0,05) maupun implementasi akuntansi hijau (beta = 0,329; p < 0,05). Lebih lanjut, CSR bertindak sebagai mediator parsial dalam hubungan antara literasi keuangan hijau dan praktik akuntansi hijau (beta = 0,159; p < 0,05), dengan nilai R sebesar 0,521. Hasil ini menekankan pentingnya strategis untuk meningkatkan literasi keuangan yang berorientasi lingkungan dan memperkuat komitmen CSR untuk memajukan praktik akuntansi berkelanjutan di UMKM. Detailed Description of the Research Paper Detailed Research Description The proposed research, titled “Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Societal Transformation: Integrating Educational Modernization, Workforce Reskilling, Digital Innovation, and Responsible AI Governance,” examines the growing influence of artificial intelligence on education, employment, institutional development, and socioeconomic progress. The study addresses the need for individuals, educational institutions, industries, and governments to adapt to emerging AI technologies through improved digital literacy, curriculum modernization, professional training, and responsible technology governance. Rather than treating AI exclusively as an automation tool, the research considers it a broader technological capability that can support knowledge creation, decision-making, scientific research, industrial productivity, and innovation. A major focus of the study is the transformation of educational systems. It examines how AI literacy, computational thinking, practical digital skills, and discipline-specific applications can be incorporated into academic curricula. It also emphasizes the continuing importance of teachers, independent reasoning, academic integrity, and human supervision in AI-supported learning environments. The research further investigates the relationship between artificial intelligence and employment. It distinguishes between the automation of individual tasks and the elimination of entire occupations, highlighting the importance of workforce reskilling, lifelong learning, and human–AI collaboration. It discusses how organizations can prepare employees for changing job requirements while addressing the risks of unequal opportunities and employment disruption. Another important dimension is the development of regional innovation ecosystems through collaboration among universities, industries, research institutions, startups, and government agencies. Such collaboration can support technology transfer, applied research, entrepreneurship, and the development of AI-enabled solutions to practical challenges. The study also considers the ethical and institutional challenges associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, system reliability, cybersecurity, digital inequality, and accountability. It proposes an Integrated Responsible AI Adoption Framework based on five interconnected dimensions: AI literacy, education and skill development, institutional modernization, responsible governance, and innovation-driven opportunity creation. Methodologically, the paper adopts a conceptual and descriptive approach, synthesizing established perspectives on AI governance, digital transformation, workforce development, and educational technology. The framework is intended to provide a foundation for future empirical investigations involving students, educators, employers, policymakers, and technology professionals. The study concludes that the effective use of artificial intelligence depends not only on technological advancement but also on human capability, institutional preparedness, inclusive access, and responsible implementation. title: Building Supply Chain Resilience in India’s Pharmaceutical Industry: API Import Dependence and the Production Linked Incentive Response
summary: India is a leading global supplier of generic medicines, yet its pharmaceutical industry depends heavily on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), key starting materials and drug intermediates, most of them from China. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed this vulnerability: prices of essential APIs rose sharply in early 2020, and India restricted exports of 26 APIs and formulations. This paper uses a qualitative case study design to examine how this vulnerability arose, how it was revealed by the pandemic, and how Indian policy has responded. Drawing on official trade data, parliamentary replies, government reports and the supply chain resilience literature, the study analyses the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for bulk drugs, the PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals and the Bulk Drug Parks scheme. The analysis shows that China accounted for roughly two-thirds of India’s bulk drug and intermediate imports by value between 2019–20 and 2022–23. The policy response has created new domestic capacity, and by early 2026 the government reported import substitution of about Rs 2,190 crore under the bulk drug scheme, which remains modest relative to total imports. The paper proposes a Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Resilience Framework and draws implications for managers and policymakers.

title: Predicting supply chain bottlenecks with real-time data: a bibliometric review of transport and logistics research from 2016 to 2025
summary: Abstract Supply chain bottlenecks are critical constraints that disrupt the smooth flow of goods, often triggering delays that cascade through interconnected processes and weaken overall resilience. In an era of digital transformation, the ability to anticipate such constraints through real-time data and predictive analytics has become increasingly important, yet the existing literature remains fragmented across transportation, logistics, and information systems, leaving conceptual boundaries blurred and practical insights underdeveloped. Addressing this gap, we conducted a bibliometric review of 3638 Scopus-indexed publications from 2016 to 2025, using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer to analyse publication patterns, keyword clusters, and thematic evolution. The findings reveal a strong concentration in intelligent transportation systems, with traffic congestion emerging as the most frequent theme, and four clusters identified around traffic management and detection, congestion and travel-time modelling, data infrastructure and analytics, and short-horizon flow control. A clear shift is observed between 2016–2020 and 2021–2025, marked by the growing prominence of machine learning and deep learning approaches. The study contributes by distinguishing transport-level prediction from supply chain-level bottleneck management. It further proposes a research agenda that emphasises cross-context validation, prediction-to-action integration, and explicit tests of forecast usefulness, thereby offering both theoretical clarity and practical guidance for strengthening supply chain performance.

title: Green Production and ESG in Türkiye’s Textile Sector: Implications for Export Competitiveness
summary: This study examines how ESG-linked green production practices are integrated into the strategies of textile firms in Türkiye operating within EU-oriented value chains and explores their firm-level implications for export competitiveness. The study uses a qualitative multiple-case design based on semi-structured interviews with senior decision-makers from 15 textile firms conducted in November–December 2025. The data were analyzed through iterative thematic coding supported by NVivo. The findings show that green transformation involves both technological practices, particularly in dyeing, wastewater management, and resource efficiency, and organizational responses such as reporting, certification, and supplier coordination. Export-related implications emerged inductively and were mainly associated with EU buyer retention, order continuity, audit and tender eligibility, and commercial positioning. Anticipated regulatory risks and value-chain compliance pressures were distinguished from reported market-related implications. The study contributes to the international trade and sustainability literature by linking socio-technical adaptation to market access and competitive positioning within buyer-driven export value chains.

title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
summary: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, leagility, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints.

title: The Mechanism of Digital Economy Development on Energy Intensity under the “Dual Carbon” Goals
summary: Reducing energy intensity has became important in the context of the “dual carbon” goals. Panel data were collected from 30 provinces in China during the period of 2011-2020 to investigate how the digital economy affects energy intensity and the mechanisms underlies. The empirical findings indicate that digital economy development significantly lowers energy intensity. A series of robustness checks confirm that this result is not coincidental. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the energy-reduction effect is more pronounced in non-resource-based provinces and the western region, while varying degrees of heterogeneity are observed in resource‑based provinces and the eastern and central regions. This paper elucidates the intrinsic mechanisms through which the digital economy enhances energy efficiency at the provincial level, providing empirical support and practical insights for promoting coordinated development of digitalization and greening under the “dual carbon” goals, as well as for formulating region‑specific energy transition policies.

title: SMART BUILDINGS AND ESG COMPLIANCE: A CASE STUDY OF CHINESE HIGH-RISE DEVELOPMENTS
summary: China's green building sector has become the world's largest, with the Chinese mainland ranking first globally in LEED certifications for the ninth consecutive year and its smart building market projected to more than double from $96.3 billion in 2025 to $206.4 billion by 2031. This article examines how smart building technologies support Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) compliance in Chinese high-rise developments, using Shanghai Tower as an illustrative case. The analysis finds that environmental gains from smart systems are well documented and substantial, with reported energy and water savings of 15–50% depending on intervention type, while social and governance dimensions remain comparatively underdeveloped, constrained by a “triple institutional dilemma” of carbon lock-in, human-capital alienation, and ambiguous governance structures in China's construction sector. The article concludes that smart building technology is necessary but not sufficient for full ESG compliance, and that governance frameworks — not sensors — are the binding constraint on China's high-rise sustainability transition.

title: Sustainable Supply Chain Management Practices and Performance of Food and Beverage Manufacturing Firms in Nairobi City County, Kenya.
summary: The food and beverage manufacturing sector operates in an increasingly uncertain supply chain environment characterized by resource scarcity, environmental degradation, rising regulatory pressure and growing consumer demand for environmentally responsible products. Sustainable supply chain management has emerged as an important approach through which firms can reduce environmental risk while achieving profitability and market share objectives. However, the uptake of sustainable practices among food and beverage manufacturers in Kenya remains inconsistent, and many firms are yet to realize the full performance benefits of these practices. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to establish the influence of sustainable supply chain management practices on the performance of food and beverage manufacturing firms in Nairobi City County, Kenya. It examined four practices, namely sustainable sourcing, reverse logistics, eco-innovation and sustainable packaging. The study was anchored on the Resource Dependence Theory, Systems Theory, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Circular Economy Theory. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, targeting 95 food and beverage manufacturing firms in Nairobi City County listed by the Kenya Association of Manufacturers, with supply chain managers and procurement officers as the units of observation. A sample of 128 respondents was determined using the Yamane formula and selected through stratified random sampling. Primary data were collected using a self-administered structured questionnaire, which was pilot tested on 12 respondents; all Cronbach’s alpha coefficients exceeded 0.70. Data were analysed using SPSS version 28 through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. A total of 110 questionnaires were returned, a response rate of 85.9%. The findings revealed that the four practices jointly explained 52.1% of the variation in performance. Eco-innovation had the strongest influence on performance, followed by sustainable sourcing, reverse logistics and sustainable packaging, all of which were positive and statistically significant. The study concluded that sustainable supply chain management practices are significant drivers of the performance of food and beverage manufacturing firms. The study therefore recommends that firms should prioritize organically or sustainably certified inputs and maintain supplier sustainability performance databases; streamline returns processes and integrate recycling programmes into supply chain operations; align ecological product design with consumer demand; and strengthen reusable packaging return systems, recycling labels and supplier monitoring for non-hazardous packaging materials.

title: The Digital Transformation of HigherEducation in Poland: Current Status and Prospects for Development
summary: This article addresses issues related to the digital transformation of higher education in Poland. Currently, one of the fundamental prerequisites for its effective and efficient operation is the implementation of integrated management systems based on data analysis, as well as the digitization of teaching and administrative processes. Accordingly, the aim of this study was to analyze and evaluate the key regulatory conditions governing the digitization of higher education in Poland under the current legal framework, while identifying prospects for future development. It was found that digital transformation is undoubtedly one of the key imperatives for development and a fundamental structural challenge for contemporary higher education institutions. Taking into account the legal regulations in force in Poland, it can be concluded that in the area of higher education administration, the state, through legal norms, is driving a digital transformation toward the computerization of specific aspects of the activities of the Minister of Science and Higher Education and the supporting apparatus under his authority, and toward the consolidation of these processes over time. At the same time, in the area of higher education administration, the state, through legal norms, does not impose obligations but rather creates a normative framework for digital transformation by individual institutions of higher education, recognizing their autonomy within legal limits.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN RAIL FREIGHT: LEVERAGING IOT AND BLOCKCHAIN FOR OPTIMIZING THE CHINA-EUROPE EXPRESS RAILWAY
summary: The China-Europe Express Railway has grown into a corridor carrying more than three million TEUs annually, yet its continued efficiency gains increasingly depend on digital rather than physical infrastructure. This article examines how the Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain are being applied to optimize the corridor's cargo visibility, customs clearance, and documentation processes. Drawing on recent industry and academic literature, the study finds that IoT applications — from satellite-based container tracking to wagon-condition sensors — are already deployed at meaningful scale, while blockchain applications remain comparatively nascent, concentrated in customs and trade-documentation pilots. The two technologies are shown to be complementary rather than substitutable: IoT generates the real-time operational data that blockchain-based systems require to create trustworthy, shared, and auditable records among the corridor's many independent railway administrations, customs authorities, and freight forwarders. The analysis concludes that sequencing IoT investment ahead of blockchain deployment is the more pragmatic near-term pathway.

title: A Digital Transformation Initiative for the Jolo Land Transportation Office
summary: This study examined the challenges, perceived advantages, and implementation requirements of digital transformation in licensing procedures at the Jolo Land Transportation Office (LTO), Sulu, Philippines. Anchored in the Technology Acceptance Model, Diffusion of Innovations theory, and socio-technical perspectives, it used a descriptive mixed-methods design combining stakeholder questionnaires, key-informant interviews, and document review. Participants included licensing applicants, LTO personnel, and community stakeholders; the source manuscript did not state a definitive total number of respondents. Descriptive statistics (weighted means and standard deviations) and qualitative coding were used to organize the evidence. Respondents rated document verification and data-accessibility challenges as very challenging (M = 3.58), alongside workforce and infrastructure constraints (M = 3.63) and data-security and ethical issues (M = 3.67). They agreed with anticipated digitalization benefits for document verification (M = 4.07), workforce development (M = 4.17), and infrastructure resilience and ethical governance (M = 4.27). Ratings were similarly favorable for proposed functionality (M = 4.05), operational readiness (M = 4.11), and infrastructure safeguards (M = 4.05). Interview coding identified process delays, system transition, service improvement, and continuous system enhancement as interconnected priorities. These findings support a phased, security-conscious, and inclusive licensing modernization model combining digital record management, staff capacity building, reliable infrastructure, and accessible service channels. Because reported benefits were predominantly prospective or perception-based, the findings do not establish actual reductions in processing times or improvements in applicant satisfaction after implementation.

title: Artificial intelligence adoption and ethical governance in sustainable financial decision making among listed firms in the Gulf Cooperation Council
summary: This study advances the intelligent-accounting literature by examining how AI-based tools embedded in accounting systems shape sustainable financial decision-making in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) listed firms. Using a panel of 52 listed firms across the six GCC states over 2015–2024, the study apply the two-step system generalized method of moments (system GMM) to address dynamic persistence and endogeneity. Sustainable financial decision-making (SFD-M), proxied by ESG performance, is dynamic and path dependent: the lagged dependent variable is positive and significant across specifications. AI tools adoption (AI-TA) has a positive effect on SFD-M that is marginally significant, offering suggestive rather than conclusive evidence that AI-enabled accounting systems support more sustainability-oriented decisions. The digitalization index (DI) is insignificant in baseline models, indicating that digital infrastructure alone does not improve sustainability outcomes without complementary capabilities. Mechanism tests provide only weak evidence that AI-TA and DI raise accounting intelligence (AC-INT) or data quality (DQ), proxied by earnings quality; the estimated technology–mechanism links are positive in sign for AI-TA but statistically insignificant. In the full dynamic model neither DQ nor AC-INT is a significant direct driver of SFD-M, and bootstrapped indirect effects through both mechanisms are statistically indistinguishable from zero, so the data do not support the proposed mediation. Moderation analysis shows that ethical governance (EG) significantly strengthens the sustainability payoff of accounting intelligence and data quality: the AC-INT×EG and DQ×EG interactions are positive and significant even though the corresponding main effects are not. By integrating direct, mediated, and moderated pathways within a dynamic panel, the study offers theory-based and practical guidance for AI-driven sustainable finance in emerging markets.

title: Management Control Systems in the Context of Digital Transformation: A Theoretical and Empirical Review
summary: Digital transformation is reconfiguring management control systems (MCS) through new forms of information processing, automation, coordination, and decision-making. This study exami-nes this relationship through an integrative review and relational thematic synthesis of 16 documents selected from specialized literature. The evidence was organized into six clusters: MCS architecture and reconfiguration, digital dynamic capabilities, digitalization and data-driven control, governance and decentralization, controllers and digital competencies, and artificial intelligence and algorithmic control. Co-occurrence analysis identified digitalization and data-driven control as the main connecting node, particularly through its relationships with controller competencies and governance. Four cross-cutting tensions also emerged: stability--adaptation, centralization--decentralization, automation--professional judgment, and efficiency--explainability. The findings indicate that digital transformation does not replace management control systems; rather, it reshapes their architecture, functions, professional roles, and governance mechanisms.

title: Financial reporting quality, corporate law compliance, and shareholder value: Evidence from Saudi joint-stock firms
summary: The subject of discussion in this research paper is the effect of reporting quality on shareholder value in Saudi joint stock companies. Though there are some international papers on the influence of audit oversight and international financial reporting standards (IFRS) on reporting quality, there is a scarcity of empirical studies on the topic among Saudi joint stock companies (Doan et al., 2026; Osemy, 2025). It should be noted that financial statements are developed with the interests of shareholders, the key users of accounting information, in mind (Alshammari, 2025; Al Sharif, 2026; Lampiris et al., 2025; Tran & Dang, 2026). Data were collected via structured questionnaires from 504 people. Then, these data were analyzed using techniques such as descriptive statistics, t-tests, and simple linear regression. Good-quality financial reporting has a positive influence on decision-making of the shareholders, increases their confidence, and allows maximizing their profit. Simple linear regression analysis reveals that there is a significant positive correlation between the two variables under consideration. The findings of the study are consistent with Vision 2030, as they increase financial transparency and corporate governance in Saudi capital markets. Concerning this issue, Doan et al. (2026) and Osemy (2025) point to the absence of empirical studies among Saudi joint stock companies on the influence of IFRS and audit oversight. Furthermore, Alshammari (2025), Al Sharif (2026), Lampiris et al. (2025), and Tran and Dang (2026) confirm that financial statements serve the interests of shareholders, the key users of accounting information.

title: Do ESG‐Oriented Common Institutional Investors Reduce ESG Strategic Dissimilarity? Evidence From Multinational Firms
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether ESG‐oriented common institutional ownership reduces strategic dissimilarity among multinational rival firms. Prior research primarily examined common ownership in relation to competition, firm performance, ESG disclosure, and ESG ratings, with limited attention to its role in shaping strategic ESG convergence among commonly owned firms. Using a global sample of 7766 listed firms and 110,490 firm‐dyad‐year observations from 2010 to 2024, we employ a dynamic panel system GMM approach to investigate this relationship. The findings show that ESG‐oriented common institutional ownership significantly reduces ESG strategic dissimilarity, indicating that such ownership promotes convergence rather than differentiation in firms' ESG strategies. This convergence effect is stronger in industries with high ESG materiality, where ESG issues are more visible, financially relevant, and reputationally sensitive. Furthermore, additional analyses show that reputational risk avoidance and ESG disclosure coordination explain this convergence effect, while cross‐national distance shapes the effectiveness of ESG coordination across countries. This study contributes to common ownership, institutional investors, and ESG strategy research by showing that ESG‐oriented common institutional ownership serves as a portfolio‐level governance mechanism that promotes ESG coherence among multinational rivals.

title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY AND TAX AVOIDANCE REGULATION: A TWO-WAY INTERPLAY
summary: Abstract Corporate social responsibility, increasingly framed through environmental, social and governance practices, remains under-integrated within corporate taxation. This article analyses the two-way interplay between responsibility norms and the legal regulation of tax avoidance. It argues that responsibility is neither wholly extra-legal nor purely voluntary, while tax law alone is constrained by definitional indeterminacy, limits of legal design and enforcement, structural arbitrage opportunities, business lobbying and weaknesses in public accountability. Responsibility norms can strengthen tax governance and transparency; legal rules can, in turn, discipline responsibility initiatives through disclosure and accountability. Their interaction provides a more credible framework for constraining aggressive avoidance and strengthening corporate accountability in taxation.

title: Corporate Governance in India
summary: Corporate Governance is the system of processes, principles, and policies through which a company is directed and controlled, and its failure can bring down even profitable companies. This article explains why investor protection a legal concern is as well as a financial one. It examines how the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 give legal force to the principles of accountability and transparency. Using the collapse of IL&FS and the Satyam scandal as case studies, it shows how weak board oversight, ineffective audit committees and inadequate internal controls allow financial misreporting to go undetected, and it traces the regulatory response that followed Satyam. This article argues that India has considerably strengthened its legal framework, but that corporate governance ultimately depends on accountability in practice and not merely in rule.

title: Entrepreneurial opportunity evaluation for financial technology decision
summary: Abstract Purpose Financial technology (FinTech) is increasingly associated with digital transformation and broader sustainability-oriented economic objectives. Although previous studies have extensively examined technological and organizational determinants of FinTech adoption, less attention has been given to the entrepreneurial cognitive processes associated with strategic technology investment decisions. This study examines the relationship between Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation (EOE) and Financial Technology Decisions (FTD) among Thai financial institutions and assesses the mediating roles of Risk Re-Categorization (RRC), Financing Constraints Alleviation (FCA), Information Asymmetry Reduction (IAR), and Operational Efficiency Incentives (OEI). Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted among Chief Financial Officers (CFOs) of firms listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET). Data were collected from 32 financial institutions and analyzed using Hayes’ PROCESS macro with bias corrected bootstrapping to examine the proposed mediation model. Findings The findings indicate that Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation significantly influences Financial Technology Decisions both directly and indirectly. Risk Re Categorization, Financing Constraints Alleviation, and Information Asymmetry Reduction significantly mediate this relationship, whereas Operational Efficiency Incentives do not exhibit a significant mediating effect. Among the mediators, Financing Constraints Alleviation demonstrates the strongest indirect influence, suggesting that improved access to financial resources constitutes a primary strategic motivation for FinTech adoption within Thai financial institutions. Research limitations/implications The study is based on a relatively small sample of publicly listed financial institutions in Thailand, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. Future research should employ longitudinal and cross-country designs to examine how entrepreneurial opportunity evaluation influences digital transformation across different institutional contexts. Originality/value This study extends entrepreneurial cognition research by examining Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation as an antecedent associated with strategic FinTech decisions. By integrating Resource Dependence Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, it evaluates organizational mechanisms through which entrepreneurial evaluation is statistically linked to technology decisions. The sustainability discussion is framed as a broader implication rather than a directly measured outcome: the observed mechanisms may be relevant to financial inclusion, information transparency, organizational resilience, and sustainability-oriented digital transformation, particularly in relation to SDGs 8 and 9.

title: Board Gender Diversity, Capital Structure, and Earnings Management: The Moderating Role of the Audit Committee
summary: Background: Recurring financial-reporting concerns in Indonesia and mixed prior evidence on the governance determinants of earnings management create a need to clarify when monitoring mechanisms constrain managerial reporting discretion. The study addresses the gap concerning whether audit committee meeting intensity conditions the relationships of board gender diversity and leverage with earnings management in an emerging-market consumer-sector setting. Objective: This study examines the associations of board gender diversity and capital structure with earnings management and tests audit committee meeting intensity as a moderator. Methods: The unit of analysis is 266 firm-year observations (133 consumer cyclical and consumer non-cyclical firms × 2 years) listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2023–2024 and selected purposively. A centered moderated regression was estimated in EViews 13 using Stubben’s discretionary-revenue measure and White cross-section robust standard errors. Results: Board gender diversity is negatively associated with earnings management (β = −0.0244; p = 0.0158), whereas leverage is positively associated with it (β = 0.0500; p < 0.001). The board-gender-diversity × audit-committee interaction is not significant (β = −0.0050; p = 0.2674), while the leverage × audit-committee interaction is negative and significant (β = −0.0218; p < 0.001). Conclusion: Audit committee meeting intensity appears to constrain leverage-related reporting pressure but does not significantly amplify the board-diversity pathway. The study contributes a conditional governance perspective in which monitoring mechanisms are matched to the source of reporting risk.

title: Digital transformation and career sustainability in rapidly reforming healthcare systems: thriving at work as a boundary condition
summary: Purpose Digital transformation is reshaping healthcare systems, yet limited evidence exists on how such large-scale technological change influences the sustainability of healthcare professionals' careers. This study examines the relationship between digital transformation and career outcomes in healthcare and investigates thriving at work as a psychological boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the socially embedded model of thriving and career construction theory, the study adopts a time-lagged design. Survey data were collected from healthcare workers working in hospitals undergoing rapid digital reform across two waves separated by six weeks. The data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and moderated regression techniques. Findings The results show that digital transformation is positively associated with career adaptability, career optimism, and subjective career success. Thriving significantly moderates these relationships. Among the Saudi healthcare workers studied, the positive associations between digital transformation and career outcomes were stronger at higher levels of thriving and weaker at lower levels of thriving. Research limitations/implications The study relies on a two-wave time-lagged design and non-probability sampling within the Saudi healthcare system, which limits causal inference and the generalizability of findings. Practical implications The findings suggest that healthcare leaders may benefit from complementing investments in digital infrastructure with managerial practices that support clinicians' vitality and learning to sustain workforce effectiveness. Originality/value This study advances healthcare organization and management scholarship by conceptualizing career outcomes as system-embedded indicators of workforce sustainability under digital reform. By identifying thriving as a boundary condition, the study provides insight into how thriving may condition the association between digital transformation and career outcomes among Saudi healthcare workers.

title: IMPROVING CSR REPORTING AND AUDIT ASSURANCE IN ARMENIAN COMMERCIAL ORGANIZATIONS: METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES, DOUBLE MATERIALITY, AND ESG INDICATORS
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has become an integral component of sustainable business development and corporate accountability (United Nations Global Compact, 2023). Modern organizations are increasingly expected to disclose not only financial information but also environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance indicators to meet the growing expectations of investors, regulators, and other stakeholders (IFRS Foundation, 2023). In this context, the quality, comparability, and reliability of sustainability-related information depend significantly on the existence of effective reporting and assurance mechanisms (GRI, 2021). Furthermore, recent developments in global sustainability regulation, particularly the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), have strengthened the demand for transparent sustainability disclosures and independent assurance practices (European Commission, 2023; EFRAG, 2023).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting Information Systems: Enhancing Financial Reporting Accuracy, Audit Efficiency, and Decision-Making
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is shaping Accounting Information Systems (AIS) by allowing firms to automate mundane accounting tasks, contribute to managerial decision-making, enhance auditing processes, and increase the accuracy of financial reporting. Traditional AIS are mostly created on the basis of specified rules, human data processing and traditional internal controls. This can restrict their capacity to review vast quantities of sophisticated financial data in a timely manner. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies including machine learning, natural language processing, robotic process automation and predictive analytics offer fresh answers to these limitations. This paper critically reviews the role of AI in AIS. It’s about the effect of artificial intelligence on the accuracy of financial statements, the effectiveness of auditing, fraud detection and the development of strategic options. It is a conceptual approach to research that involves a comprehensive review of relevant literacy and decision-making frameworks and professional standards. The paper said artificial intelligence can enhance transaction classification, identify financial anomalies, speed audit data analysis and provide real-time financial insights. However, some of these benefits depend on cybersecurity, governance, expert monitoring, data integrity and system stability. The essay also discusses other issues such as algorithmic bias, explanations, implementation costs, privacy problems, and the ever-expanding skill set that accountants must acquire. Therefore, AI should not replace the professional judgment of accountants, but rather used as a tool to assist them in making those decisions. The report concludes with a call for a shared governance model, a call for technical innovation along with human accountability, ethical safeguards and ongoing oversight. The results of this research are useful for organizations who want to enhance their accounting procedures in a more advanced and data driven commercial environment.

title: How Does Digital Innovation Drive Corporate Sustainability? A Systematic Literature Review
summary: This study systematically reviews recent empirical evidence on the relationship between digital innovation and corporate sustainability. Using the Scopus database, the review identified 231 articles through the search string (“digital” OR “digital innovation” OR “digitalization”) AND “corporate sustainability”. After applying inclusion criteria covering publications from 2023 to 2026, English-language journal articles, open access availability, and quantitative empirical design, 49 articles were retained for synthesis. The findings show that digital innovation is conceptualized through multiple forms, including digital transformation, digital finance, artificial intelligence, digital accounting, supply chain digitalization, digital leadership, executives’ digital attention, and digital–green integration. Most studies indicate that digital innovation positively contributes to ESG performance, corporate sustainability performance, sustainable development performance, and sustainability efficiency. However, the relationship is not automatic or universally linear. Its effect depends on mediating mechanisms such as green innovation, operational efficiency, financing access, information transparency, supply chain coordination, resource orchestration, and governance improvement. The review also identifies important boundary conditions, including digital maturity, organizational capability, leadership support, digital infrastructure, environmental regulation, and institutional quality. This study contributes by organizing fragmented empirical evidence into an integrated thematic framework and highlighting future research directions for global scholars examining digital transformation, ESG practices, and sustainability-oriented corporate strategy worldwide.

title: Industry 4.0 adoption for supply chain performance in Tunisian companies
summary: Goal: This study aims to investigate the direct and indirect effects of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) on supply chain performance (SCP) in Tunisian firms, by testing the mediating role of supply chain resilience (SCRes) and the moderating role of supply chain visibility (SCV). Design/Methodology/Approach: The analysis collected data from 81 Tunisian companies across diverse sectors, including manufacturing, agri-food, pharmaceutical, and other activities using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the theoretical hypotheses. Smart PLS 4.0 is the statistical software used in this survey. Results: Supply chain resilience significantly mediates this relationship, indicating that I4.0’s full performance benefits are contingent upon strengthening resilience capabilities. Additionally, supply chain visibility positively moderates the link between I4.0 and resilience, demonstrating that higher visibility amplifies the positive effect of I4.0 on SCRes. These findings emphasize that I4.0 generates maximum impact only when combined with resilience and visibility efforts. Limitations of the investigation: This study has five main limitations (cross-sectional design, moderate sample size, self-reported measures, focus on only three I4.0 technologies, and single-country context), which future research should address through longitudinal designs, larger samples, objective data, and cross-country comparisons. Practical implications: This research offers an actionable plan for Tunisia's industrial evolution, showing how a strategic focus on I4.0 -driven resilience and visibility can directly boost the private sector's competitiveness, strengthen the national economy, and ensure a more prosperous position in the global market. Originality/Value: This study extends Qader et al. (2022) by providing the first empirical examination of their integrated I4.0, resilience, visibility, and performance framework in an African emerging economy (Tunisia). While the conceptual model and hypotheses are adapted from Qader et al. (2022), we contribute by validating the framework in a context characterized by fragmented logistics, small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) dominance, and high information asymmetry, conditions that may amplify the importance of visibility mechanisms. The findings offer context-specific insights for other emerging economies.

summary: This study conducted an intra-disciplinary review exploring how multinational enterprises (MNEs) contribute to sustainability in local markets within the fields of international business (IB) and strategy.It comprehensively examines four key themes of corporate social responsibility, economic (regional) development, social performance, and environmental sustainability of MNEs.By doing so, it seeks to consolidate fragmented findings from existing independent studies while broadening understanding through problematizing assumptions made in research.In addition, it sheds light on the complexities that MNEs face to address sustainability challenges, and how to strategically integrate economic, social, and environmental goals while adapting to global and local pressures.In turn, we propose new research directions and draw implications for MNEs in addressing grand challenges.Overall, this study contributes to deepening sustainability research in IB and strategy fields, and provides valuable insights for MNEs' sustainable business practice.

summary: This thesis explores ways to improve the institutional foundation and digital panel-data monitoring infrastructure for assessing corporate governance, ownership structure, and dividend policy as determinants of share market value in Uzbek joint-stock companies (JSCs). Based on an analysis of statutory norms and Republican Stock Exchange "Toshkent" panel data for 95 listed issuers, it is shown that while governance norms exist, board independence and dividend payout parameters are not substantively linked to state ownership concentration and minority valuation discounts. A conditional sequence, the "single issuer code – single governance-dividend parameter – single data source" principle, and five readiness indicators are substantiated.

title: Omnichannel, Resilience, and Artificial Intelligence in the Supply Chain: a Bibliometric Analysis (2019–2026) and an Integrative Framework
summary: Objective: To map the intellectual and thematic structure of research on omnichannel (2019–2026) and, based on the identified themes, propose an integrative framework that connects omnichannel, supply chain resilience, and artificial intelligence (AI) without multiplying risks. Methods: A mixed-methods study combining bibliometric analysis—according to Donthu et al. (2021), based on a corpus of 2,869 journal articles extracted from the OpenAlex open-access database and selected using PRISMA—with performance analysis and scientific mapping, and the deductive construction of a conceptual framework based on the identified gaps. Results and Conclusion: Output grew from 99 articles (2019) to 813 (2025), totaling 26,161 citations; The United States, Indonesia, China, and India lead; and the thematic structure reveals a core focused on customer experience and channel integration, an axis centered on supply chain and logistics, and a cluster related to digital transformation, while AI and resilience remain emerging areas. In light of this gap, a four-layer framework is proposed—data sources, real-time integration, intelligence, and decision-making, under cross-functional governance—from which three management principles are derived: visibility with verification prior to automation; AI as augmentation, not replacement; and the primacy of competencies and coordination. Research Implications: The study provides a current overview of the field and a structured tool for managing the risks created by integration, with socio-environmental and sector-specific implications. Originality/Value: It links empirical evidence on the structure of the field to a conceptual framework, articulating omnichannel, resilience, and AI—which are usually treated in isolation—and reframing integration as a system that simultaneously mitigates and generates risks.
