title: Assessing greenhouse gas emissions in the cassava flour supply chain: Evidence from small‐scale production units
summary: Abstract This study applies Life Cycle Assessment to quantify greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the cassava flour production chain, from cultivation to final processing. Primary data were collected in 2023 from two small‐scale artisanal facilities in Northeast Brazil (CF‐I and CF‐II). The functional unit was the annual processing of 10,400 kg of cassava roots. CF‐I separates its output into cassava flour and wet starch, whereas CF‐II retains the starch in the flour. Agricultural and machinery operations, electricity, firewood, and water consumption were accounted for. Total carbon footprints were evaluated using IPCC 2021 GWP 100a characterization factors. Reported GHG totals account for upstream supply chain burdens and non‐CO 2 combustion gases, excluding biogenic CO 2 emissions under the carbon‐neutrality convention. Overall GHG emissions were 2585.15 kg CO 2 ‐eq/year for CF‐I and 1532.47 kg CO 2 ‐eq/year for CF‐II. The highest contribution is associated with firewood consumption for flour roasting, followed by fossil fuel consumption during root transportation. Cassava peel and sieving residues used as animal feed substitutes yielded avoided emissions. Comparative analysis revealed significant differences in resource use efficiency between facilities. Scenario analysis showed that adopting CF‐I's lower‐emission transport configuration could reduce CF‐II transport emissions by 31.15%, while adopting CF‐II's metal‐pan roasting configuration could reduce roasting‐related emissions in CF‐I by 60.00% (yielding a 53.89% reduction in overall facility emissions).

title: Legal Aspects of Fintech in India
summary: Fintech has widened the access to payments, credit and investment in India, but its characteristics of speed and anonymity have also enabled rising financial fraud and unauthorized advice. This paper asks whether India's legal framework is equipped enough to adequately protect the consumers on digital financial platforms. Rather than treating Fintech as a single category, it analyses two regulators: the Reserve Bank of India, which governs payments and digital lending, and the Securities and Exchange Board of India, which governs robo-advisory, algorithmic trading and unregistered "finfluencers". Using a doctrinal methodology of research, it examines statutes, directions, regulations and circulars, alongside fraud data and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. It finds that regulation has followed market development rather than anticipating them, that several activities fit poorly within existing regulatory categories, and that regulation alone, without enforcement, cannot curb fraud without enforcement, awareness and coordination. The most significant gaps between regimes, including fragmented grievance redressal and overlapping breach-reporting duties. The paper recommends closer inter-regulatory coordination and a dedicated robo-advisory framework, proportionate influencer registration and clearer alignment with the DPDP Act.

title: Corporate Storytelling through CSR Disclosures During and After COVID-19: Evidence from Indian Pharmaceutical Firms
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the priorities of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and communication practices, especially in the pharmaceutical industry. This paper explores the ways in which major Indian pharmaceutical firms used CSR disclosures as strategic narrative in the midst of the pandemic and after it. CSR parts of Annual Reports, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports (BRSR), and other disclosures of eleven companies (2020-2023) were content analysed, using thematic analysis, sentiment analysis, and word frequency, with the help of a mixed-method content analysis. Findings show that there is a distinct shift in the narrative of pandemic relief and healthcare support to sustainability, ESG integration, digital health, and long-term development programs in the post-pandemic era. Mostly positive sentiment indicates the attempts to preserve legitimacy and confidence of stakeholders. The results underscore CSR reporting as a strategic communication tool that is not necessarily related to regulatory compliance.

title: The more confident the more digital? A study of the mechanisms of CEO overconfidence on corporate digital transformation
summary: Purpose This study examines how CEO overconfidence influences corporate digital transformation and explores the cognitive-behavioral mechanisms underlying this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2024, this study constructs a language-based measure of CEO overconfidence from CEOs' personal social media posts and their directly attributable statements reported in publicly available sources. Two-way fixed-effects models are employed to examine the relationship between CEO overconfidence and corporate digital transformation, supplemented by robustness checks including alternative measures, additional fixed effects, instrumental variable analyses and Heckman two-stage analysis. Findings The results show that CEO overconfidence is positively associated with firms' digital transformation. This effect operates primarily through entrepreneurial orientation and strategic risk-taking, with the two mechanisms forming a sequential mediating relationship. Furthermore, the positive effect of CEO overconfidence on digital transformation is strengthened when CEOs possess an IT background and greater CEO power, as well as when firms have higher levels of resource slack and operate in regions with higher levels of market development, but is weakened in state-owned enterprises. Originality/value This study advances upper echelons theory by developing a commitment-based account of how CEO overconfidence shapes strategic change under uncertainty and by specifying a cognition–posture–action process through which executive cognition is translated into firm-level digital transformation. Methodologically, it introduces a language-based measure of CEO overconfidence derived from CEOs' linguistic expressions, offering an alternative approach to capturing executive cognition beyond traditional financial proxies.

title: La performance de l'Investissement Socialement Responsable(ISR) au Maroc : Une analyse comparative au sein de la Bourse des Valeurs de Casablanca(BVC)
summary: RÉSUMÉ : L’Investissement socialement responsable (ISR) se considère comme la forme la plus dominante de la finance durable. Il est le reflet de la RSE au sein des marchés financiers. En effet, ce type d’investissement vise à réconcilier la performance financière, à l’instar de l’investissement traditionnel, et la performance extra-financière basée sur la prise en compte des aspects Environnementaux, Sociaux et de la Gouvernance (ESG). Les apports théoriques ainsi que les études empiriques antérieures ont montré une absence d’un consensus évident autour de la performance de l’ISR. Si certains auteurs soutiennent sa surperformance, d’autres insistent sur sa sous performance. De même, certains d’autres déclarent qu’il n’est ni sous ni surperformant, c’est-à-dire qu’il est neutre. Le présent travail de recherche a pour objet d’analyser la performance de l’ISR dans le contexte marocain. En particulier, d’étudier la performance de l’indice le Casablanca ESG10 en comparaison avec celle de l’indice MASI et de l’indice MSI20 (MADEX). D’après les résultats, le Casablanca ESG10 sous performe ses homologues conventionnels en terme du rendement absolu et du rendement ajusté au risque. Les résultats obtenus n’ont aucune significativité statistique. Mots clés : Investissement socialement responsable, Responsabilité sociétale de l’entreprise, critères ESG, performance financière, performance extra-financière. ABSTRACT: Socially Responsible Investment (SRI) is considered the most dominant form of sustainable finance. It is the reflection of CSR within the financial markets. Indeed, this type of investment aims to reconcile financial performance (FP), like traditional investment, and extra-financial performance based on the consideration of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) aspects. Theoretical contributions as well as previous empirical studies have shown a lack of clear consensus around SRI performance. While there are some who support its outperformance, there are also others who insist on its underperformance. Similarly, some others state that it is neither under-nor over-performing, in other words that is neutral. The purpose of this research is to analyze the performance of SRI in the Moroccan context. In particular, to study the performance of the Casablanca ESG10 index in comparison with MASI index and MSI20 (MADEX) index. According to the results, the Casablanca ESG10 underperforms its conventional counterparts in terms of absolute return and risk-adjusted return. The results obtained have no statistical significance. Key words: Socially Responsible Investment, Corporate Social Responsibility, ESG criteria, financial.

title: A hybrid data prioritization and neural network framework for cost‑optimized supply chain management
summary: The increasing complexity and volatility of modern supply chains necessitate intelligent decision-support systems that can efficiently process vast amounts of operational data while maintaining computational tractability. Traditional supply chain optimization models often fail to leverage the inherent structure of operational data, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and increased costs. Existing approaches in supply chain management (SCM) typically treat forecasting and optimization as separate stages, with data preprocessing methods, including computational sorting, serving merely as preliminary steps without any formal integration into the decision-making framework. This separation results in missed opportunities for improving operational efficiency and responsiveness. This study proposes a novel hybrid framework that formally integrates a data prioritization mechanism inspired by computational sorting principles with a neural network (NN)-based forecasting model within a unified cost-minimization mathematical programming framework. The prioritization mechanism generates a composite priority score (δij) derived from demand, cost, and inventory attributes, which is then embedded as an upper bound on assignment variables in the optimization model to guide resource allocation decisions. The framework is validated through comprehensive numerical experiments across 10 diverse supply chain scenarios, with each instance replicated 30 times to ensure statistical reliability. The primary scientific contribution lies in the mathematical formalization of the data prioritization process and its integration as operational constraints in the optimization model, rather than treating sorting as a mere preprocessing step. This formal linkage between data characteristics and optimization decisions distinguishes our approach from prior studies. Computational results, validated through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) with F = 28.4 and p < 0.001, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance. The Hybrid Framework reduces Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 40.7% (from 178.50 to 105.80) compared to Single Sorting methods, and achieves a 12.1% reduction in average total cost compared to Data Science methods (from 14,528 to 12,769) and a 22.2% reduction compared to Single Sorting methods (from 16,407 to 12,769). The framework delivers a service level of 94.2%, significantly higher than the 86.6% achieved by Single Sorting and 89.6% by Data Science methods. Sensitivity analysis confirms robustness, maintaining service levels above 90% even under high demand variability (CV = 0.8), while scalability analysis demonstrates near-linear growth in computation time, with large-scale instances (50 × 20) solved in approximately 15 min (920 s). These findings underscore the practical potential of the proposed approach as a robust decision-support tool for strategic and tactical supply chain planning, offering managers a data-driven pathway to improve operational resilience and efficiency. title: Enforcing Financial Reporting Integrity Through Finite State Machine-Driven Transaction Lifecycles in Web-Based Sales Order Management Systems
summary: Financial ledger accuracy depends heavily on strict control over transaction states and lifecycle progression. In dynamic retail environments, erroneous transactions require systematic handling to prevent reporting distortion. This paper introduces a Finite State Machine (FSM) approach to govern transaction lifecycles—transitioning strictly from creation, through optional cancellation (VOID), to completion. By enforcing transactional state boundaries and implementing automated query filters, the system ensures that voided entries are entirely segregated from financial statements, guaranteeing immutable audit trails and precise financial reporting. title: Improved European native seed supply chains are essential for the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation
summary: Abstract To support the implementation of the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (NRR), there is an unprecedented need to scale up ecosystem restoration, which requires radical improvements to the European seed supply chain, especially for herbaceous species. The fundamental tradeoff between the need for local provenance and climate resilience, as well as practical constraints on seed availability, generates a bottleneck for restoration practice and may jeopardize the implementation of the NRR. Here, we overview the current legislative context for plant reproductive material, assess the status of native seed supply, and propose institutional and operational solutions to strengthen seed supply chains in Europe. We call for the adoption of the concept of Native Seed and Restoration Centres (NSRCs) to boost seed supply chains. We outline the main functions and responsibilities of NSRCs, and highlight the short‐ to mid‐term actions that are crucial for enhancing the availability and use of native seeds.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND THE EVOLUTION OF EMPLOYMENT MODELS: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR EMERGING ECONOMIES
summary: This thesis examines how digital transformation reshapes employment models in emerging economies. Using conceptual and comparative analysis, it distinguishes changes in workplace tasks, digital job matching, and the governance of employment relationships. Particular attention is paid to remote work and platform-mediated employment, including opportunities for labor market participation and risks related to contractual uncertainty and social protection. The study proposes an analytical framework linking technological adoption, institutional readiness, and job quality. It outlines policy priorities for improving workforce adaptability and inclusive employment outcomes.

title: Integration of Construction Supply Chain Management and Project Controls for Improved Cost Performance in Mega Projects
summary: Cost escalation in megaprojects is frequently recorded as a project-controls problem although a material proportion of its antecedents originates outside the conventional cost ledger: in supplier capacity, procurement decisions, fabrication readiness, delivery uncertainty and poorly sequenced site work. This integrative review examines how construction supply chain management (CSCM) can be connected to project controls to improve the timeliness and reliability of cost decisions. Thirty DOI-identifiable publications dated 2020–2025 provide the core analytical literature, complemented by critical examination of the managerial mechanisms linking procurement and production information to schedule and cost forecasts. The review adopts thematic synthesis rather than a statistical meta-analysis because the publications differ in design, context and outcome measures. Four interdependent mechanisms emerge: a common work-package data structure; supplier-informed lookahead and change control; reconciliation of earned value, commitments and remaining exposure; and governance that assigns accountability for corrective action. An integrated control architecture and an explicitly hypothetical, internally reconciled numerical example illustrate how cost signals can change when upstream commitments and schedule consequences become visible. The argument is not that technology independently creates savings, but that decision quality improves when trusted supply-chain evidence is translated into actionable project forecasts. The paper develops research propositions and a validation agenda for complex, multi-contractor delivery environments, while identifying contractual, data-quality and organizational conditions under which integration may fail.

title: Designing a Smart Contract-Based Decentralized Marketplace for Vegetarian Food Supply Chains: Pilot Evaluation of VegeChain in Indonesia
summary: Vegetarian food supply chains in Indonesia are constrained by fragmented intermediation, opaque quality information and slow settlement, which erode producer margins, weaken consumer confidence and slow the adoption of plant-forward dietary programmes such as Meatless, Balanced, Green (MBG). This study designed, prototyped and evaluated VegeChain, a decentralized marketplace in which Ethereum-compatible smart contracts execute automated market maker pricing with perishability-aware time decay, sensor-assisted quality verification, reputation-weighted trust scoring and escrow-based settlement. A design science research process combined architecture design, mathematical modelling of multi-objective supply chain efficiency, and empirical validation through a 90-day pilot in 12 Indonesian districts with 456 supply chain stakeholders, complemented by load testing with 25,000 concurrent users. Relative to the conventional multi-tier chain, the prototype improved supply chain efficiency by 35%, reduced transaction costs by 34% and food waste by 28%, shortened payment cycles from 42 to 3 days, raised end-to-end traceability from 12% to 97% and increased consumer trust by 42% (p < 0.001). The Byzantine fault tolerant consensus sustained 99.1% accuracy under peak load, gas optimisation lowered execution costs by 67% and quality verification reached 98.3% accuracy. The results provide a reference architecture and deployment roadmap for blockchain-enabled vegetarian food markets.

title: Supply chain coordination in contract farming under yield uncertainty and alternative agricultural subsidy policies
summary: Food grain subsidies and contract farming are two important institutional arrangements for stabilizing agricultural production and improving farmers' incomes. However, the effectiveness of these policies and organizational arrangements depends critically on the interaction between subsidy mechanisms and supply chain contracts. To examine this interaction, we develop a Stackelberg game model of the operational decisions and coordination of a contract farming supply chain under two major agricultural subsidy programs: the Target Price (TP) program and the Producer Direct (PD) program. Our analysis yields several important insights. First, both subsidy schemes increase the company's profit relative to the no-subsidy benchmark. For farmers, however, the TP scheme does not always yield higher profits than the no-subsidy case. When the farmer's production cost coefficient is relatively low, the subsidy induces substantial expansion of planted acreage. As the Stackelberg leader, the company responds by substantially reducing the wholesale price. This adjustment redistributes part of the benefits generated by the target-price subsidy from farmers to the company. Second, the traditional wholesale-price contract fails to coordinate the contract farming supply chain in the presence of government subsidies. To address this issue, we propose a “wholesale price + fixed transfer” contract that effectively coordinates the supply chain. Third, our analysis reveals an important welfare implication: despite double marginalization, the wholesale-price contract may generate higher social welfare than the coordinating contract under the PD program when the subsidy level exceeds a certain threshold. These findings enrich the literature on agricultural subsidy policies and contract farming supply chains. They also offer useful guidance for designing subsidy mechanisms and coordination contracts that improve economic efficiency and social welfare in agricultural systems.

title: Navigating the digital: university business model patterns and aligning digital transformation strategies
summary: Purpose Digital transformation poses various challenges for universities, necessitating adjustments to business models and strategic positioning. We aim to identify university business model patterns and derive matching digital transformation strategy options, providing universities with a structured basis for aligning transformation efforts with their strategic orientation. Design/methodology/approach Based on an adapted Business Model Canvas for universities, we qualitatively analyze business model data collected from the 30 largest German universities. Data were structured into 59 subcategories across nine business model elements and analyzed through cross-case analysis in ten iterative workshops, combining quantitative and qualitative data to derive patterns and corresponding strategy options. Findings Five university business model patterns exist: three research-oriented (excellence, entrepreneurial and domain-specific) and two education-oriented (teacher training and education), including a distinct distance-learning subset. Research-oriented patterns show higher third-party and state funding and more research staff, while education-oriented patterns emphasize teaching scale. Matching Digital Transformation Strategy options were derived across four dimensions: technology use, value creation, structural change and financial aspects. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to German universities, which may influence the generalizability of the findings to other higher education contexts. Further research should examine our business model patterns in other countries and education systems. Practical implications Findings guide university management in aligning digital transformation strategies with their specific business model pattern rather than standardized approaches, requiring coordinated governance across research, teaching and administration. Social implications Findings suggest uniform funding and governance approaches may not reflect universities' heterogeneous orientations, calling for more differentiated, equitable higher education policy. Originality/value This study offers one of the first empirically derived typologies of university business models, systematically linking distinct patterns to matching digital transformation strategy options.

title: Digital transformation in healthcare: a systematic and bibliometric review of strategies, policies, barriers, and benefits
summary: Digital transformation (DT) in healthcare has traditionally been conceptualized through models that privilege either technological or organizational perspectives. However, this study shows that DT cannot be understood as a linear or purely technical process but rather as a dynamic adjustment among policy frameworks, organizational capabilities, and technological change. To capture this complexity, we conducted a systematic and integrative review that combined bibliometric mapping and a grounded qualitative synthesis of literature published between 2010 and 2025, guided by three research questions: (RQ1) What are the key themes and trends in healthcare DT? (RQ2) What policy-level barriers and enablers shape its development? and (RQ3) What strategic challenges and benefits influence DT in healthcare institutions? Findings reveal that prevailing models—such as the HIMSS EMRAM and McKinsey 7S frameworks—offer valuable benchmarks but remain limited by static and technocentric assumptions. Building on these insights, this study proposes an integrated framework grounded in Social Systems Theory, which conceptualizes DT as an adaptive system characterized by iterative feedback, learning, and recalibration across policy, organizational, and technological domains. The framework contributes both a theoretical advancement toward an evolutionary understanding of DT and a practical roadmap for policymakers and healthcare managers aiming to build sustainable, interoperable, and human-centered health systems.

title: Integration of ESG principles into the project management
summary: The article is devoted to the integration of ESG principles into project management in the context of Russia’s changing regulatory framework. The study analyses the challenges of implementing sustainable development principles throughout the project lifecycle, changes in the functions of project managers, and models of interaction with stakeholders. The necessity of transitioning from classical management models to a paradigm that combines economic efficiency, environmental safety, social responsibility, and corporate policy is substantiated. A typology of ESG risks and a methodology for their quantitative assessment based on an integral indicator of expected losses are proposed. The authors have developed a model of the relationship between classical groups of project management processes and aspects of sustainable development. The aim of the study is to systematize approaches to integrating ESG principles into project management and to formulate practical recommendations considering new regulatory requirements. The methodological framework is based on an analysis of the regulatory framework, a comparative analysis of international standards, as well as a synthesis of best practices and identified challenges, followed by the development of practical recommendations. Sustainable development is becoming a fundamental factor in the long-term competitiveness of companies, and the successful integration of ESG principles requires the consolidation of efforts by business, the state, and society, the develop-ment of flexible planning systems, and the improvement of project managers’ qualifications.

title: Third Party Supply Chain Planning Operating Models and the Separation of Decision Rights Inventory Ownership and Systems
summary: This paper explains how third-party planning arrangements differ when planning work, final decisions, inventory ownership and financial risk are assigned to different parties. It addresses the limits of describing an arrangement only as outsourced, integrated or vendor-managed. The paper develops a conceptual framework through a selective synthesis of research on vendor-managed inventory, consignment, collaborative planning, system integration and logistics outsourcing. It defines the main design choices, combines them into reference models and uses logical comparisons to explain their possible consequences. Moving demand, inventory, and supply to a provider does not necessarily move approval rights or inventory risk. The framework identifies four sources of difficulty: – A gap between recommendations and approval, – A gap between decisions and available information, – A gap between ownership and financial exposure, and – A gap between local objectives and network needs. Five propositions explain how these gaps may affect responsiveness, oversight and coordination under stated conditions. The paper provides a common way to describe alternative planning arrangements, identifies four gaps between assigned responsibilities and the means to fulfil them, and develops five conditional propositions. These contributions support comparison at the level of individual decisions.

Based on systematic conceptual analysis, it distinguishes foundational digital literacy, occupation-specific competencies, and transferable analytical capabilities. The study examines how changing workplace tasks generate skills mismatches and why continuous training requires coordination between employers and education providers. A conceptual framework is proposed for linking competency assessment, modular learning, and employment outcomes. Recommendations focus on demand-oriented reskilling, verifiable skill acquisition, and inclusive access to lifelong learning.

title: Systemic Greenwashing in Sustainable Finance: How EU Regulations Launder Carbon-Intensive Assets Into Sustainable Investments
summary: This article introduces the concept of systemic greenwashing. Drawing on original empirical analysis of “green” investment funds with the European Union’s highest sustainability classification, it addresses the striking paradox that portfolios classified by EU regulations as “green” are drastically more carbon intensive than those with no sustainability objectives, despite no evidence of falsified disclosures. Combining close analysis of EU regulations with detailed case studies of corporations that dominate “green” portfolios, the article demonstrates that greenwashing in this context is not the result of corporate deception or weak enforcement, but is instead performed by regulatory processes which reclassify carbon-intensive corporate activities into sustainable contributions to decarbonisation. The implications for criminology are significant, reframing greenwashing as a structural form of state-corporate harm.

title: Abnormal Production Activity in an Emerging Market: Short-Term Accounting Gains, Inventory Accumulation, and Cash-Flow Consequences
summary: This study examines the economic consequences of abnormal production activity among Vietnamese listed manufacturing firms by investigating its effects on accounting performance, inventory accumulation, and future operating cash flows. Using an unbalanced panel of 243 firms over the period 2016–2024, abnormal production activity is estimated using the normal production cost model [2], and the hypotheses are tested with firm fixed-effects regressions. The results show that abnormal production activity improves short-term accounting performance but does not enhance longer-term performance, operating cash flows, or market-based performance. It also increases subsequent inventory intensity, while firms with high inventory intensity experience weaker future operating cash flows. These findings suggest that the accounting benefits of abnormal production activity are temporary and accompanied by inventory-related operating costs, providing new evidence on the economic consequences of production-based real earnings management in an emerging market.

Results show financial sharing significantly improves accounting comparability; digital transformation strengthens this effect whereas controlling shareholder tunneling produces restraining influence, with earnings volatility acting as a partial mediator. title: ESG Performance, Disclosure and Environmental Intensity: Implications for Profitability in Emerging Market Energy Companies
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between ESG performance, environmental intensity, greenwashing, and profitability in energy companies operating in emerging markets. An unbalanced panel of 95 publicly listed companies from Asia, Europe, and Latin America over 2015–2024 is analyzed using dynamic panel‐data models. ESG performance is found to be positively associated with profitability, while environmental intensity exerts a negative effect. The positive impact of ESG performance is stronger in larger companies, suggesting that organizational scale enhances the benefits derived from sustainability initiatives. Greenwashing, measured as the gap between ESG disclosure and ESG performance, is negatively associated with profitability, indicating that sustainability claims are penalized when they are not supported by actual ESG outcomes. The results also show that the COVID‐19 pandemic and the Russia‐Ukraine conflict reduced the profitability penalty associated with greenwashing. The findings highlight the importance of disclosure credibility and ESG performance in emission‐intensive industries.

title: Perceived Effectiveness of Finance and Accounts Practices in a Precision Automotive Components Manufacturer: A Questionnaire-Based Study with a Proposed Finance–Operations MIS Dashboard
summary: Manufacturing finance functions are expected to do more than record transactions; they must supply timely, accurate and decision-relevant information to production, procurement and senior management. This study examines the perceived effectiveness of finance and accounts (F&A) practices in a precision automotive components manufacturer in Jamshedpur, India, using a fifteen-item, five-point Likert questionnaire that covers seven dimensions: financial reporting and accounting controls, taxation and compliance, budgeting and variance analysis, management information system (MIS) and decision support, cost analysis, digital integration and automation, and people and coordination. The research context is built from industry data and a review of recent literature on the digitalisation of management accounting, enterprise resource planning (ERP) and business intelligence, and Industry 4.0 in automotive manufacturing. Descriptive statistics and cross-tabulation are applied to a simulated demonstration dataset of 48 respondent records. The dataset is disclosed as simulated throughout and is intended to illustrate the analytical method, not to evidence the actual performance of any organisation. In the demonstration dataset, financial reporting and accounting controls recorded the highest theme mean (4.17), followed by taxation and compliance (3.98), cost analysis (3.88), people and coordination (3.85), MIS and decision support (3.83), budgeting and variance analysis (3.66) and digital integration and automation (3.49); the overall mean was 3.85. Perceived MIS timeliness differed by role, with managers rating it higher than executives. The paper proposes a phased Finance–Operations MIS dashboard that prioritises data integration, driver-based budgeting and exception-based alerts, and it offers a replicable instrument for future studies with authenticated data. title: Technology, Organization, and Environment in Digital Transformation: The Role of Employees' Digital Readiness as a Moderating Variable at Benyamin Guluh Kolaka Regional Hospital
summary: Dvancing modern healthcare relies heavily on digital transformation, a process driven not merely by deploying technological tools, but also by ensuring structural adaptability and workforce preparedness. This research investigates how Technology, Organization, and Environment influence Digital Transformation, while analyzing Employee Digital Readiness as a moderating factor within Benyamin Guluh Kolaka Regional General Hospital. Utilizing a quantitative cross- sectional framework, 200 participants were chosen via purposive sampling from a total cohort of 534 staff members. A 20-item instrument on a five-point Likert scale was administered, with data evaluated through Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4 and bootstrapping techniques. The results demonstrate that Technology, Organization, and Environment each exert a statistically significant positive effect on Digital Transformation. Additionally, Employee Digital Readiness demonstrates a direct positive association with Digital Transformation and enhances the structural connections between Technology, Organization, Environment, and Digital Transformation. With an ????2 coefficient of 0.335, the predictive model accounts for 33.5% of the variance observed in Digital Transformation, underscoring the critical interplay between technical infrastructure, institutional backing, external drivers, and staff preparedness in driving hospital digitalization.

title: Substance versus symbolism: how ESG dimensions relate to financial performance in family firms
summary: Purpose This study examines how ESG performance, environmental innovation, exposure to ESG controversies, and internal governance mechanisms are associated with the financial performance of listed family firms. Socioemotional wealth (SEW) is used as an interpretive lens rather than measured as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach A near-balanced panel of 83 firms from the Global 500 Family Business Index over 2016–2023 (662 firm-year observations) is analysed using two-way fixed effects models with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors. Robustness checks include clustered and bootstrap inference, lagged specifications and an alternative measure of controversy. Regional differences are examined in an exploratory pooled interaction model. Findings ESG performance is positively associated with Tobin's Q but not with accounting metrics. Environmental innovation is associated with higher ROE, although this association does not survive conservative inference. Controversy exposure is associated with lower ROA and ROE. The only result robust to every inference procedure concerns governance: where boards reach a critical mass of female directors, the market valuation of ESG is reversed rather than amplified. Practical implications ESG score optimisation should not be treated as a route to accounting value in family firms. Boards should not assume that formal gender diversity reinforces the credibility of ESG commitments. Originality/value The study integrates ESG performance, environmental innovation, controversy exposure, and board governance into a single framework for large family firms and shows that board composition operates as a boundary condition of the ESG market signal.

title: Responsible Data and AI Practices in Engineering Education: Preparing Graduates for Digital Transformation in Industrial Processes
summary: INTRODUCTION: As artificial intelligence (AI) tools become increasingly integrated into higher education, understanding how engineering students perceive and apply principles of academic integrity, data integrity and responsible AI use has become increasingly important. OBJECTIVES: This study investigates how master’s engineering students perceive and apply principles of academic integrity, data integrity, and responsible AI use. It also explores the potential relevance of these practices for the development of competencies associated with participation in data-driven and AI-enabled professional environments. METHODS: A mixed-methods approach was employed using the PEDRA questionnaire (Perceptions on Ethics and Development of Responsibility in Academia), developed by the authors. The instrument was designed to explore students’ perceptions, experiences, and ethical reasoning regarding academic integrity and responsible research practices. The analysis focused on two questionnaire items addressing the influence of academic honesty on data use and the frequency of AI tool use in academic activities. The study involved master’s engineering students from two higher education institutions. RESULTS: Based on the 48 complete responses analysed, the findings indicate awareness of data integrity principles, particularly regarding anonymity, confidentiality, informed consent, and rigorous data analysis. Ethical referencing and transparency in data handling were mentioned less frequently, suggesting areas for further educational support. Regarding AI adoption, 21 of 48 respondents (43.8%) reported occasional use of AI tools, reflecting a cautious and exploratory approach. Descriptive differences in AI use were observed across age and gender groups, with female respondents being more likely to explore AI while maintaining ethical awareness, although these findings should be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: The study highlights the importance of integrating responsible data and AI practices into engineering education. The results suggest that developing students’ capacity to use data and AI critically, transparently, and ethically may support the development of competencies associated with responsible participation in increasingly digital and AI-enabled environments. The PEDRA questionnaire demonstrates potential as an exploratory and diagnostic instrument for identifying educational needs related to academic integrity, responsible AI use, data integrity, and trustworthy digital practice.

title: Balancing Mineral Extraction and Environmental Regulation: An Analysis of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 and the 2023 Amendment
summary: In recent past we have witnessed India's mineral sector being reshaped into a competitive commercial market, instead of its traditional image as a discretionary licensing system. The repeatedly amended Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, with the recent amendments of 2015 and 2023, presently allocates mineral franchise largely through auctions, and has made available exploration and critical minerals to a wide private presence. This paper asks whether the amended Act, read with the surrounding environmental framework, balances mineral extraction against environmental protection legal system. It argues that the reforms have redesigned mining as a market while leaving environmental compliance outside the ambit of the incentive structure of that market, so that concession holders, who have the greatest control over environmental outcomes, face weak financial and governance incentives to comply. Using a doctrinal method, the paper tracks the statutory evolution of the Act, inspects the 2023 Amendment, reviews the judicial response, and then evaluates three management law mechanisms: auction design, the District Mineral Foundation alongside corporate social responsibility, and sustainability disclosure. It identifies five problems and suggests a corresponding reform for each: baseline screening at the exploration stage, earlier environmental scrutiny in the allocation process, environmental weighting in auctions, community-centred use of mining levies, and mine-level disclosure. summary: Metalcraft micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Bali contribute to the island’s craft economy, yet their transition to environmentally responsible production may be constrained by limited technical resources and uneven environmental capabilities. The estimated relationships are positive and statistically significant, and Green Innovation partially mediates the relationships between both capability constructs and Sustainable Performance. Green Creative Self-Efficacy has numerically larger path coefficients than Green Skill for Green Innovation and Sustainable Performance; this coefficient ordering is interpreted descriptively because a formal between-coefficient difference test was not reported. IPMA identifies environmental awareness and pollution-control facility deployment as specific improvement priorities. The study extends MSME sustainability research by linking an individual-level cognitive capability with operational innovation in a traditional craft setting. For practice, the results support combining practical green-skills training with confidence-building problem-solving activities and affordable, context-appropriate pollution-control and waste-management measures.

title: Accounting Practices and Financial Performance of Quoted Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria: Evidence from Revenue Recognition, Inventory Valuation and Depreciation Practices
summary: This study examines the relationship between selected accounting practices and the financial performance of quoted manufacturing firms in Nigeria. The study focuses on revenue recognition practices, inventory valuation methods and depreciation practices, with return on assets (ROA), operating profit margin (OPM) and return on equity (ROE) serving as the respective performance indicators. An ex-post facto design was adopted, using secondary information derived from the published financial reports of selected quoted manufacturing firms. The reported sample comprises Lafarge Africa Plc, BUA Group and Dangote Group. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and simple regression models were employed. The reported results indicate positive and statistically significant relationships between revenue recognition practices and ROA (R = 0.748; R² = 0.559; β = 0.580; t = 5.999; p < 0.001), inventory valuation methods and OPM (R = 0.786; R² = 0.618; β = 0.691; t = 6.118; p & lt; 0.001), and depreciation practices and ROE (R = 0.804; R² = 0.646; β = 0.742; t = 6.761; p & lt; 0.001). The study recommends stronger compliance with applicable financial reporting requirements, robust internal controls over revenue recognition, effective inventory systems, and periodic review of depreciation policies. title: Factors affecting audit quality in government internal audit institutions: The roles of independence, workload, and auditor specialization
summary: Audit quality plays a critical role in strengthening government internal oversight and enhancing accountability in the management of public resources. Nevertheless, recurring audit findings indicate that maintaining high-quality audits remains a challenge within APIP institutions. This study examines the effects of auditor independence, workload, and auditor specialization on audit quality among auditors of the Inspectorate General of the Ministry of Public Works. A quantitative approach was employed using primary data collected through a survey of 109 auditors. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that auditor independence and auditor specialization positively and significantly influence audit quality, whereas workload has a significant negative effect. Among the examined factors, auditor independence emerged as the strongest determinant of audit quality. These findings suggest that improving audit quality requires not only the enhancement of technical competencies but also the preservation of professional objectivity and effective workload management. This study contributes to the public sector auditing literature by providing empirical evidence on the determinants of audit quality within government internal audit institutions, particularly in the infrastructure sector, which remains underexplored in previous studies.

title: Strategic Educational Leadership and Management Practices as Predictors of Institutional Effectiveness: A Framework for AI-Enabled Digital Transformation in Higher Education
summary: This study examined the predictive influence of strategic educational leadership and management practices on institutional effectiveness in selected higher education institutions and developed an artificial intelligence-enabled digital transformation framework based on the findings. Specifically, it assessed the levels of strategic educational leadership, management practices, and institutional effectiveness and determined whether leadership and management practices significantly predicted institutional effectiveness. A quantitative, non-experimental predictive-correlational research design was employed, involving 136 academic administrators selected through total enumeration. Data were collected using a validated and reliability-tested survey questionnaire and analyzed through weighted mean, standard deviation, and multiple linear regression at a 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed high levels of strategic educational leadership (4.32), management practices (4.30), and institutional effectiveness (4.29). Regression analysis showed a strong predictive relationship, with a correlation coefficient of 0.870 and a coefficient of determination of 0.756, indicating that the independent variables explained 75.6% of the variance in institutional effectiveness. Both strategic educational leadership and management practices significantly and positively predicted institutional effectiveness, with regression coefficients of 0.431 and 0.440, respectively. The findings highlight the importance of effective leadership and sound management in improving institutional performance. The study concludes that strengthening these practices can enhance institutional effectiveness in higher education institutions. Based on the findings, an artificial intelligence-enabled digital transformation framework was developed to integrate strategic leadership, effective management, and artificial intelligence-driven innovations. The framework aims to support evidence-based decision-making, improve organizational processes, strengthen quality assurance, and promote continuous institutional improvement. Its implementation may help higher education institutions achieve sustainable effectiveness and respond to the evolving demands of digital education.

summary: The new update to Schedule M under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules is dated December 28, 2023. title: The shadow of ESG: how sustainable investing affects stock ownership and delisting

title: Dynamic carbon emissions and liquidity management under policy transition risks
summary: Liquidity is central to long-run green innovation under policy transition risk. We develop a dynamic model of carbon emissions and liquidity management for financially constrained firms under carbon policy transition risk. Our results show that greater policy transition risk promotes green innovation when cash liquidity is abundant, but reduces it when constrained. Furthermore, our paper reveals an inverted U-shaped relationship between policy stringency and green innovation. Moderate policy stringency promotes green innovation as the innovation-benefit effect dominates, whereas excessive stringency strengthens the liquidity-cost effect and discourages innovation by tightening firms' liquidity constraints. This finding provides theoretical support for the Porter Hypothesis and offers a potential explanation for the conflicting empirical evidence on the relationship between green innovation and environmental regulation.

title: Personnel training for the digital construction industry: economic aspects
summary: The digital transformation of the construction industry is one of the key areas for improving the efficiency of investment and construction activities. The introduction of building information modeling technologies, digital twins, artificial intelligence, automated project management systems and other digital tools requires qualified specialists who are able to work in a digital economy. At the same time, the construction sector is facing a shortage of personnel with the necessary digital competencies. The article examines the economic aspects of personnel training for the digital construction industry, analyzes the causes of personnel shortages, examines the costs of training and corporate staff development, and evaluates the effectiveness of investments in improving employee digital literacy. Special attention is paid to the issues of interaction between educational organizations and construction companies as the main mechanism for the formation of human resources in the industry. Based on the analysis, promising models of cooperation between universities and employers are proposed, ensuring an increase in the quality of specialist training and a reduction in personnel shortages.

title: Tanggung Jawab Sosial, Etika Bisnis, dan Pemindaian Lingkungan Strategis dalam Manajemen Strategik: Sebuah Tinjauan Literatur
summary: Corporate social responsibility, business ethics, and the analysis of the strategic environment are two pillars that are often discussed separately, even though both determine the long-term sustainability of a firm within the discipline of strategic management. This study aims to synthesize recent scholarly literature examining these two pillars and to map the conceptual linkages between them. This research employs a narrative-thematic literature review method, drawing on articles published in internationally reputable journals indexed in Scopus (quartile Q1 to Q3) within the last three years (2023-2026), complemented by foundational theoretical works that continue to underpin the field. The review identifies five major themes: (1) the conceptual evolution and enduring debate surrounding corporate social responsibility; (2) the empirical relationship between social responsibility and financial performance; (3) ethical governance mechanisms, particularly whistleblowing, as instruments of organizational integrity; (4) environmental scanning and competitive strategy frameworks, particularly Porter’s Five Forces, as tools for reading the external environment; and (5) the intersection of social responsibility and industry competitiveness as a mediating pathway linking the two pillars. The findings indicate that social responsibility and environmental analysis are not two separate strategic activities, but two complementary capabilities that jointly determine a firm’s competitive advantage and organizational legitimacy. This study contributes theoretically by offering an integrative framework connecting business ethics literature with strategic analysis literature, and practically by providing managers with references for designing more comprehensive corporate strategies.

title: EFFECT OF SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS PRACTICES ON COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE OF DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS
summary: This study examined the influence of sustainable business practices on competitive advantage in deposit money banks in Calabar. The specific objectives were to determine the effect of environmental sustainability practices on customer loyalty, economic sustainability practices on profitability, corporate governance and ethical practices on brand reputation among money deposit banks. The study adopted a quantitative research design using a cross-sectional survey approach. Primary data was collected through structured questionnaires administered to employees of selected deposit money banks under study. Data was analyzed using simple linear regression analysis at a 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed that environmental sustainability practices have a significant positive effect on customer loyalty. Economic sustainability practices were found to have a significant positive effect on profitability. Corporate governance and ethical practices significantly influenced brand reputation. The results further indicated that all null hypotheses were rejected, confirming that sustainable business practices significantly enhance competitive advantage in deposit money banks. It recommended that banks should strengthen their environmental initiatives, enhance economic efficiency strategies, reinforce corporate governance systems, and expand customer-focused digital and sustainability-driven innovations.

summary: Purpose This study empirically tests the effects of effort expectancy (EE), performance expectancy (PE), social influence (SI), facilitating conditions (FC), attitude, subjective norm (SN), perceived behavioral control (PBC), and lifestyle of hedonic consumption (LOHC) on behavioral intention to use FinTech lending (BIUFL) and actual usage of FinTech lending (AUFL). Design/methodology/approach This study utilized convenience sampling to select 350 university students from Indonesia. Data were collected using an online questionnaire. Data were analyzed using variance-based structural equation modeling with WarpPLS. Findings Our study found that PE, attitude, PBC, and LOHC were essential factors in BIUFL. We report that the EE, SI, FC, and SN do not affect BIUFL. Finally, BIUFL was found to positively influence AUFL. Practical implications Regulators enhance supervision by issuing regulations that set strict requirements for Gen Z to access FinTech lending, particularly regarding prospective customers' ability to repay credit, and add parental consent as an additional requirement for Gen Z. title: The Evolution of Islamic Finance: Contractual Continuity, Institutional Transformation, and the Search for Sharia Substance
summary: Islamic finance has expanded from classical trade-based mechanisms into a global financial architecture with total assets exceeding US$3 trillion. While existing literature extensively documents its chronological progression, critical analysis regarding whether modern financial engineering preserves the economic substance of classical risk-sharing remains fragmented. This study adopts a qualitative historical-documentary and comparative thematic approach to evaluate the transformation of Islamic finance from its normative foundations to contemporary fintech innovations. We introduce a five-dimensional analytical framework, comparing Classical Foundations, Modern Forms, Continuity Mechanisms, Transformation Dynamics, and Sharia/Ethical Implications, to examine how classical contracts (Mudarabah, Musharakah, Bay’ al-Salam) have evolved into modern capital market instruments (Sukuk, Takaful, trade finance). Our findings indicate that while contractual continuity remains robust at the formal compliance level, institutional transformation has led to a significant reliance on debt-like replication (Tawarruq) and benchmark pricing linked to conventional interest rates. Consequently, modern innovations often prioritize legal form over economic substance (Maqasid al-Shariah).

title: Working Capital Alchemy: Unveiling Triple Effects and Accounting Best Practices for Global Enterprise Success in Economic Shifts
summary: Abstract This study examines how working capital mastery drives working capital optimization across receivables and credit management, cash flow and payables management, and liquidity and contingency management, while assessing the moderating role of working capital resilience. Using survey data from 202 finance professionals across manufacturing, hospitality, and tourism, and commercial sectors in Kosovo (2023–2025), the study applies factor analysis, structural equation modeling, and moderation analysis. The findings show that stronger working capital mastery consistently improves all dimensions of working capital optimization. Working capital resilience selectively moderates these relationships, weakening the effects on receivables and liquidity management while slightly strengthening the effects on cash flow and payables management. Overall, the results highlight that aligning working capital mastery with resilience is critical for financial performance, operational efficiency, and adaptability during economic shifts.

title: Do ESG Metrics Influence Stock Returns in Southeast Asia? Panel, Quantile, and HAC-Robust Evidence
summary: This paper aims to determine whether the process of stock return follows the performance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices of publicly listed companies in Southeast Asia. By using panel data on corporate ESG practices, the paper employed fixed-effects regression and quantile regression. In addition, standard errors were corrected using Newey–West heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent (HAC) to derive robust estimates on the mean and distribution of stock returns. The results of the fixed-effects and quantile regression revealed that there was no significant relationship between the overall ESG score and stock return. In addition, the results of the adjusted model showed the absence of significance after correcting for serial correlation and heteroskedasticity, which means that the short-run return pricing does not consider the overall ESG score. Overall, the results of the paper revealed that the ESG practices are not embedded in the short-run stock market return of Southeast Asia. In terms of methodological significance, the paper showed the importance of using panel, quantile, and HAC-based analysis in the examination of finance-based ESG practices.

title: A Strategic Pathway from ESG Management to Innovation: The Serial Mediating Roles of Absorptive Capacity and Dynamic Capability
summary: In an era of uncertainty, dynamic capabilities are recognized as an essential source of competitive advantage for firms. In this study, we examine the relationships between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) management; innovation; and the development of dynamic capabilities. Researchers have recently sought to explain ESG performance in relation to innovation and have increasingly considered the role of dynamic capabilities in this context. However, prior research has not adequately demonstrated how absorptive capacity and dynamic capability may develop through ESG management, and further examination is needed to determine whether ESG management is associated with innovation beyond incremental performance outcomes. By considering absorptive capacity and dynamic capability, we examine whether these capabilities mediate the relationship between ESG management and innovation and whether they operate sequentially. Using data from 200 Korean small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), we analyzed the relationship between ESG management and innovation using Hayes’s PROCESS MACRO to identify the mediating roles of absorptive capacity and dynamic capability. The results indicate that SMEs’ commitment to ESG policy and practices is associated with innovation through both absorptive capacity and dynamic capability. Based on these findings, we discuss innovation strategies for SMEs operating in changing environments. This study contributes to the literature theoretically by clarifying the process through which ESG management is associated with innovation via absorptive capacity and dynamic capability. From a practical perspective, it suggests that, for resource-constrained SMEs, ESG management may serve as a strategic tool rather than merely a regulatory requirement, helping firms respond to uncertainty and strengthen their competitive advantage.

title: EXPLORATION OF THE EXPERIENCES OF SARI LAUT BUSINESS ACTORS IN THE APPLICATION OF FINANCIAL TECHNOLOGY AND PRODUCT INNOVATION TO SUPPORT FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
summary: This study aims to explore the experiences of seafood entrepreneurs in Wua-Wua and Mandonga Districts, Kendari City, in implementing financial technology (fintech) and product innovation to support financial performance. The study used a qualitative approach with a phenomenological design to understand the experiences, meanings, and adaptation processes of business actors in utilizing technology and developing products. Informants were selected purposively from business actors who have used fintech and implemented product innovation, with data collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation. Data validity was checked through triangulation and member validation. checking, while the analysis was conducted using the Miles and Huberman model through data condensation, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results of the study indicate that fintech adoption is primarily related to transaction needs, financial recording, and access to financing. Adoption is influenced by user experience, perceived benefits, business needs, and the level of trust in the service. Barriers were found in literacy, security, infrastructure, and service conditions. Product innovation develops through learning from consumers, business experience, and changing market needs, but faces limitations in raw materials, production processes, and product durability. The impact on financial performance is perceived through changes in sales, cash flow, efficiency, and access to capital, although not uniformly felt. The study concludes that the benefits of fintech and product innovation are contextual and depend on the ability of business actors to integrate both with operational and market needs.

title: Enterprise Data Governance Combining Federated Transfer Learning and Security Audit
summary: Due to the problems of dispersed business data, inconsistent regulatory interpretations and limited cross-domain modeling at the enterprise level, this paper puts forward a data governance model based on federated transfer learning and security auditing. The preprocessing stage adds salted pseudonymization, entity masking, rare-category pooling, 30-minute window aggregation, and lineage/access-log feature construction to ensure reproducibility without revealing raw records. The method builds metadata, lineage, access behavior and rule-hitting features locally in each business domain and achieves cross-domain knowledge transfer via transfer gating and alignment loss. At the same time, it records summary hashing, responsible parties, policy consistency and lineage continuity in audit quality scores, adds a risk-suppression aggregation mechanism, and synchronously links the model update process to the governance traceability process. Experiments are based on financial, procurement, logistics, sales and compliance data from a large local group from January 2024 to December 2025. According to the results above, the proposed method achieves an AUC of 0.957, a macro-F1 score of 0.912, a recall of 0.926, and an audit trace completeness of 0.987. It is 2.1 and 2.3 percentage points higher than the best-performing comparative method. Extra imbalance, threshold-sensitivity and edge deployment tests show that the transfer gate reduces negative transfer in a 1:50 class imbalance, and audit-suppressed aggregation maintains real-time latency below 160ms under the tested edge configuration. Thus, cross-domain risk identification and strategy implementation can be achieved in a closed-loop manner without aggregating raw data, and a technical path for enterprise data governance that balances accuracy, compliance, and feasibility has been provided. A separate public HDFS log benchmark supplies a limited proxy stress test; it does not validate enterprise audit completeness or reproduce an accuracy advantage over FedAvg.

title: Akuntabilitas dan Transparansi Pengelolaan Zakat Nasional: Analisis Laporan Pengelolaan Zakat Nasional Tahun 2023–2025
summary: This study analyzes the accountability and transparency of national zakat management in Indonesia based on the National Zakat Management Reports for the period 2023–2025. Employing a descriptive-comparative analysis of secondary data, the study compares year-on-year growth rates, disbursement-to-collection ratios (DCR), and reporting compliance ratios across the three reporting years. Rooted in agency theory and standard Islamic accounting (PSAK 109), the study evaluates institutional expansion, collection trends, disbursement effectiveness, and mustahiq socio-economic graduation. The findings reveal a significant increase in reporting compliance (97.33% in 2025) and collection growth reaching IDR 44.70 trillion, driven by digital transformation via SIMBA and NIK integration. Highly efficient disbursement ratios (89.93%–96.55% for on-balance sheet funds) and growing auditor compliance (175 audited OPZs in 2025) demonstrate strengthened public trust and reduced agency costs. ABSTRAK Kajian ini menganalisis akuntabilitas dan transparansi pengelolaan zakat nasional di Indonesia berdasarkan Laporan Pengelolaan Zakat Nasional periode 2023–2025. Penelitian ini menggunakan analisis deskriptif-komparatif terhadap data sekunder dengan membandingkan tingkat pertumbuhan tahunan, rasio penyaluran terhadap penghimpunan (DCR), dan rasio kepatuhan pelaporan antartahun. Berlandaskan teori keagenan dan standar akuntansi syariah (PSAK 109), penelitian ini mengevaluasi ekspansi kelembagaan, tren penghimpunan, efektivitas penyaluran, serta graduasi sosio ekonomi mustahik. Hasil kajian menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan pada kepatuhan pelaporan (97,33% pada 2025) dan pertumbuhan penghimpunan hingga mencapai Rp44,70 triliun, yang didorong oleh transformasi digital melalui SIMBA dan integrasi NIK. Rasio penyaluran yang sangat efisien (89,93%–96,55% untuk dana on-balance sheet) serta peningkatan kepatuhan audit (175 OPZ diaudit pada 2025) membuktikan semakin kuatnya kepercayaan publik dan menurunnya biaya keagenan.

title: Auditing Report Order in Emergency Teleradiology Using Routine Event Logs
summary: Abstract This study aims to describe recorded report-order inversions in emergency teleradiology and assess their interpretation when assignment and active interpretation times are unavailable. We reconstructed computed tomography (CT) transmissions from July 2025 through June 2026, requiring a unique exact linkage and stable priorities. An inversion occurred when a later examination received its first recorded report before an earlier examination still unresolved at the same provider. Eligible head–abdomen pairs were analyzed using dependence-preserving intervals, an empirical conditional reference and secondary models incorporating retrieved imaging workload proxies. Among 8170 examinations, 6,051 had the standard ED urgent category. Later head CT inverted 1060/1761 earlier-abdomen pairs (60.2%; 95% confidence interval, 57.5–62.7%); later abdominal CT inverted 154/1038 earlier-head pairs (14.8%; 12.3–17.5%). Observed-minus-reference differences were − 4.5 percentage points (− 7.3 to − 1.6) and − 11.4 (− 14.2 to − 8.8). Counts were usable for 3474/3565 target examinations and 2665 pairs. Report-order asymmetry did not demonstrate preferential dispatch. Observed inversion proportions were below the empirical conditional reference probabilities. This does not establish protective scheduling. Routine exports support a descriptive audit; additional workflow events are necessary to identify mechanisms or compare dispatch policies.

title: Energy-accounting validation of QEC-assisted quantum batteries
summary: Abstract Quantum error correction (QEC) protects logical information, whereas a quantum battery is judged by the work it can deliver. We ask when a recovery operation applied during storage may be credited with protecting a battery's ergotropy. The second law bounds the average work of each recovery call from below by the change of nonequilibrium free energy it causes at bath temperature T; as a storage convention we debit the nonnegative part of this change and take the net ergotropy gain left per call as the budget for all further overhead. We apply this ledger to batteries of two to four two-level cells under collective and independent Lindblad noise, testing a coherence-restoring heuristic, the four-qubit [[4,1,2]] amplitude-damping code with two recovery completions, standard channel families, and reset channels. Every state in the code space of the [[4,1,2]] code has zero mean energy and at most half the maximal ergotropy, so a decoder that restores the code space cannot protect a fully charged battery; a completion that leaves the rest of the Hilbert space untouched avoids this bound but still loses ergotropy on a fully charged battery during storage. Unital recoveries cannot raise the ergotropy by more than the energy they supply. For four cells and inputs diagonal in the energy basis, an optimal energy-nonincreasing covariant recovery is attained by a reset channel, whose value we give in closed form and whose gain comes from removing entropy. At 10 mK and 10 GHz the tested recoveries leave at most 3.3×10⁻² energy quanta per call beyond the debit, less than one photon at the cell frequency, so any implementation that dissipates a single quantum per call beyond the debit loses ergotropy.

title: Determinants of Capital Structure Decisions Among International Takaful Operators In Malaysia: Evidence From Panel Data Analysis
summary: The capital structure decision remains an important issue in Shariah-compliant corporate finance, particularly for financial institutions whose regulatory requirements and risk-sharing structures differ from those of conventional corporations. Despite the development of Islamic finance, empirical evidence on the firm-specific determinants of leverage among foreign-owned international Takaful operators in Malaysia remains limited. This study examines the effects of firm age, firm size, liquidity, profitability, and company growth on capital structure using panel data from four foreign-owned international Takaful operators in Malaysia. Capital structure is proxied by the total-liabilities-to-total-assets ratio, which represents overall balance-sheet leverage rather than conventional interest-bearing debt alone. Audited annual financial statements were analysed using panel data regression with cluster-robust standard errors. The findings indicate that firm age, firm size, and liquidity are positively and statistically associated with leverage, whereas profitability and company growth show negative but statistically insignificant relationships. The results suggest that organizational maturity, scale, and liquidity are relevant to the liability structure of international Takaful operators, although the findings should be interpreted within the distinctive regulatory and Shariah-compliant characteristics of the industry. Overall, the evidence provides partial support for the Trade-off Theory and limited support for the Pecking Order Theory when these frameworks are adapted to the Takaful setting. The study contributes to the limited literature on capital structure in Islamic insurance and offers implications for the management of leverage, liquidity, and solvency within international Takaful operators.

title: The Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity on the Safety Performance–Firm Financial Performance Nexus: Evidence from JSE-Listed Firms
summary: The mining industry remains one of the most hazardous industries globally, with occupational injuries and fatalities imposing significant operational and financial costs on companies. Although prior research has explored the impact of workplace safety on financial performance, limited attention has been devoted to the role of board gender diversity in influencing this relationship. This paper examines the association between safety performance and firm financial performance in 46 JSE-listed mining firms, considering the moderating role of board gender diversity. This study adopted an unbalanced panel dataset covering the period 2015 to 2025. Safety performance data were obtained from sustainability reports and integrated reports, while data on financial performance and board gender diversity were obtained from annual financial reports. A fixed effects model was adopted to establish the relationship between study variables, while the two-step system generalised method of moments was used as a robustness test. This study found a statistically significant negative association between the injury frequency rate and financial performance of JSE-listed mining firms, whereas the fatality frequency rate was not significantly associated with financial performance. The findings show that board gender diversity shapes the safety performance–firm financial performance relationship. This study contributes to the occupational safety and corporate governance literature by providing evidence on the governance conditions under which safety performance influences financial performance in the South African mining sector. This study’s results suggest that JSE-listed mining firms should improve occupational safety programmes and promote greater female representation on corporate boards to improve long-term financial performance.

title: Managing climate stress for food security: the impact of rising temperatures on agricultural performance in Africa (1990–2022)
summary: Purpose Climate variation driven primarily by carbon emissions is a major driver of global warming, significantly raising Earth’s temperature. This study examines the influence of rising temperatures and carbon emissions on agricultural performance (AGP) in Africa from 1990 to 2022. The aim is to identify management policies that enhance sustainable agricultural resilience and moderate the adverse effects of climate change. Design/methodology/approach This research employs second-generation panel econometric techniques. The short- and long-run (LR) relationships between AGP, temperature, carbon emissions, sustainable finance and population growth are estimated using a Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (P-ARDL) model. Findings The results disclosed the fact that rising temperatures and carbon emissions significantly reduce AGP, highlighting the urgent need for proactive environmental management. Conversely, sustainable finance and population growth positively influence long-term AGP and food security. These variables emerge as crucial levers for climate adaptation and agricultural resilience across Africa. Practical implications Climate stress has made agricultural production more unpredictable and this threatens food security. The findings stress the need for integrated environmental and agricultural management policies. Hence, the study recommends that policymakers and financial institutions must prioritize investments in climate-smart agriculture and sustainable finance to address the challenges posed by climate variation, ensuring sustainable agricultural resilience and food security. Originality/value This study provides new evidence on the links between rising temperatures, carbon emissions, sustainable finance, population growth and AGP in Africa by jointly examining their short-run and LR dynamics within a panel framework, thereby offering policy-relevant insights for climate-resilient agricultural and financial strategies.

title: Data Factor Agglomeration and Enterprise Resilience: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from China's National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones
summary: Using the establishment of China's National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the effect of data factor agglomeration on enterprise resilience with a panel of A-share listed enterprises from 2012 to 2024. The results indicate that data factor agglomeration significantly improves enterprise resilience. The mechanism tests, interpreted alongside the theoretical analysis, provide evidence consistent with three channels: increased government subsidies, digital transformation, and stronger innovation capability. Executives' innovation awareness positively moderates the relationship between data factor agglomeration and enterprise resilience. Positive and statistically significant effects are observed among non-state-owned enterprises, enterprises in high-technology industries, and enterprises in eastern China; the corresponding estimates for state-owned enterprises, enterprises in non-high-technology industries, and enterprises in central and western China are not statistically significant. These findings suggest that policies should improve the conditions for data factor agglomeration, support enterprises' digital transformation, and account for differences in enterprises' characteristics when seeking to strengthen resilience.
